docs.title: Trainable recurrent neurons

docs.text: from tensor_optix.neuroevo import TopologyController controller = TopologyController.for_graph( graph=graph, scheduler=opt._scheduler, grow_grad_threshold=0.7, # fraction of hidden neurons with |grad| > eps required to grow prune_neuron_threshold=1e-4, # importance score below this -> prune candidate prune_edge_threshold=1e-3, # |weight| below this for prune_edge_patience episodes -> prune merge_similarity_threshold=0.95, # Pearson correlation threshold for merge ) opt.add_callback(controller) opt.run() A grow operation fires only when all three statistical signals agree: Improvement test - the score slope is not significantly positive (a corrected t-test) - i.e. gradient updates have stalled. Structure test - score residuals show significant lag-1 autocorrelation - i.e. there's unexplained structure the model isn't capturing. Capacity test - gradient utilization across hidden neurons exceeds grow_grad_threshold - i.e. existing neurons are saturated, not idle. For multi-region graphs, use TopologyController.for_brain(brain, scheduler=...) - each region gets independent signal buffers and cooldown timers, so a saturated encoder region can grow without triggering growth elsewhere.
docs.title: The topology controller

docs.text: Topology is saved alongside weights, so a checkpoint fully reconstructs the graph on load - no manual topology bookkeeping: agent.save_weights("checkpoint.pt") agent2 = make_agent(env, neuroevo=True) agent2.load_weights("checkpoint.pt") # Or skip constructing an agent entirely agent3 = GraphAgent.from_checkpoint("checkpoint.pt") agent3.act(obs) Rollback on degradation uses the same path - when the loop restores a best checkpoint, the topology at the time of that checkpoint is fully restored, even if the graph has grown or been pruned since.
docs.title: Save and load

docs.text: from tensor_optix.neuroevo import BrainNetwork, TopologyController brain = BrainNetwork() brain.add_region("sensory", sensory_graph) brain.add_region("memory", memory_graph) brain.add_region("executive", executive_graph) brain.add_pathway("sensory", "memory", n_connections=8, delay=1) brain.add_pathway("memory", "executive", n_connections=8, delay=0) controller = TopologyController.for_brain(brain, scheduler=opt._scheduler) Inter-region edges are learnable parameters; when a neuron is pruned from a region, BrainNetwork automatically removes all inter-region edges referencing it.
docs.title: BrainNetwork: composing multiple regions

docs.text: from tensor_optix.neuroevo import HebbianHook hook = HebbianHook(graph, hebbian_lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4) for step in episode: action = agent.act(obs) hook.record() obs, reward, done, _ = env.step(action) agent.learn(episode_data) hook.apply() hook.reset() HebbianHook is a LoopCallback - pass it directly via callbacks= and it wires itself automatically (it records after every act() and applies the update after each learn() ; don't call record() yourself in that case). Use HebbianHook.from_brain(brain, ...) for BrainNetwork graphs.
docs.title: Hebbian learning

docs.text: from tensor_optix.neuroevo import NeuromodulatorSignal from tensor_optix.core import RegimeDetector signal = NeuromodulatorSignal( detector=RegimeDetector(), hebbian_hook=hook, # optional agent=agent, # optional - modulates entropy_coef topology_controller=tc, # optional - modulates grow/prune thresholds ) opt = Optimizer(agent, env, callbacks=[hook, signal]) opt.run() NeuromodulatorSignal maps a RegimeDetector classification (trending / ranging / volatile) to coordinated parameter changes: trending → lower Hebbian lr and entropy (consolidate); ranging → raise Hebbian lr, lower grow threshold (explore structure); volatile → lower Hebbian lr, raise entropy (cautious plasticity).
docs.title: Neuromodulation

docs.text: # clamp mode (default): outgoing weights clamped post-step graph = NeuronGraph(dale_mode="clamp") graph.add_neuron(role="hidden", activation="relu", cell_type="excitatory") # weights >= 0 graph.add_neuron(role="hidden", activation="tanh", cell_type="inhibitory") # weights <= 0 # softplus mode: raw parameter theta, effective weight = softplus(theta) * sign # gradient-safe, no dead zone at the clamp boundary graph = NeuronGraph(dale_mode="softplus") w = graph.effective_weight(edge_id) # reads post-softplus value
docs.title: Dale's Law

docs.text: NeuronGraph runs eager by default - _raw_forward mutates Python-side neuron state, which torch.compile can't safely trace without replaying side effects. If your topology is static and you manage neuron state externally, opt in: graph.compile_forward() # one-time call; re-call after any topology mutation TopologyController calls graph.invalidate_compile() automatically after every grow/prune/merge. If you mutate the graph directly outside the controller, call it yourself.
docs.title: Compiled forward

docs.title: Reference

docs.text: make_agent(env, neuroevo=True) attaches its HebbianHook and TopologyController as agent._neuroevo_callbacks ; Optimizer wires them into the loop automatically. With RLOptimizer , pass them yourself: callbacks=agent._neuroevo_callbacks . In neuroevo_mode="feature_extractor" the graph is a recurrent feature extractor in front of SAC. Checkpoints contain the SAC networks and the graph (topology + weights) and the fixed random projection, so a restored agent reproduces the same features. The features the policy acted on are cached and reused by learn() . Restoring a checkpoint (rollback, best-weight restore at the end of run() ) rebuilds the graph in place - callbacks keep operating on the live graph.
docs.title: Things to know

docs.text: Export to ONNX pip install tensor-optix[onnx] Every BaseAgent exposes export_onnx(path) . The default implementation raises NotImplementedError ; it's overridden on all Torch agents ( TorchPPOAgent , TorchSACAgent , TorchTD3Agent , TorchDQNAgent , TorchRecurrentPPOAgent ). agent.export_onnx("policy.onnx") Only the actor (policy) network is exported - learn() , get_hyperparams() , and save_weights() are training-time operations with no place in an inference graph. For example, TorchTD3Agent.export_onnx : Export the deterministic continuous actor to ONNX. Input - "observation": (batch_size, obs_dim) float32 Output - "action": (batch_size, action_dim) float32 The actor applies tanh internally, so outputs are clipped to (-1, 1). Rescale to your environment's action bounds at deployment if required. Continuous-action agents that apply tanh internally (TD3, SAC) export actions in (-1, 1) - rescale to your environment's actual action bounds at deployment time. Discrete-action agents (PPO, DQN, Rainbow) export logits or Q-values, not sampled actions - apply argmax or your own sampling at inference time. Neuroevo agents Neuroevo's GraphAgent / RecurrentGraphAgent do not currently implement export_onnx - the dynamic, mutating topology and Python-side neuron state ( _current , history buffers) don't map cleanly onto a static ONNX graph. For neuroevo deployment, save/load the native checkpoint format ( agent.save_weights() / GraphAgent.from_checkpoint() ) instead - see Build a neuroevo agent .

docs.text: Train an RL agent This guide covers the full RLOptimizer path - validation, checkpointing, and callbacks - beyond what Quickstart shows with the simplified Optimizer wrapper. Pipelines A pipeline steps an environment (or data source), collects EpisodeData , and yields it to the agent. from tensor_optix import BatchPipeline, LivePipeline, VectorBatchPipeline import gymnasium as gym # Gymnasium env: steps continuously, no reset between windows pipeline = BatchPipeline(env=gym.make("CartPole-v1"), agent=agent, window_size=200) # External data stream: background thread with bounded queue, configurable episode boundaries pipeline = LivePipeline( data_source=MyFeed(), agent=agent, episode_boundary_fn=LivePipeline.every_n_seconds(300), ) # N parallel envs via gymnasium.vector, sync or async subprocess pipeline = VectorBatchPipeline( env_fns=[lambda: gym.make("CartPole-v1")] * 8, agent=agent, window_size=200, ) VectorBatchPipeline works with every built-in agent except TorchRecurrentPPOAgent (which keeps a single hidden state): PPO agents compute GAE per env and the off-policy agents build replay transitions per env. For PettingZoo environments see Multi-agent training . BatchPipeline does not reset the environment per window - it steps continuously and resets automatically only on terminated / truncated . window_size is the unit of training, not an environment episode. See Pipelines for the full reference, including the gym.Env method-name collision warning (don't name an env attribute close , step , reset , render , or seed ). optimal_window_size(env, algorithm) computes the formula Optimizer uses internally: clip(k * mean_episode_steps, 512, 8192) , with k=4.0 for on-policy (PPO) and k=1.0 for off-policy (SAC/TD3/DQN). from tensor_optix import optimal_window_size window = optimal_window_size(env, "PPO") # e.g. 2000 for CartPole The full loop from tensor_optix import RLOptimizer opt = RLOptimizer( agent=agent, pipeline=pipeline, # Separate validation pipeline. All checkpoint and rollback decisions use val score only. val_pipeline=val_pipeline, rollback_on_degradation=True, # Optional external scorer run at checkpoint evaluation (e.g. held-out backtest) checkpoint_score_fn=lambda a: evaluate(a, held_out_env), # Convergence parameters dormant_threshold=10, # consecutive non-improving evals -> DORMANT min_episodes_before_dormant=50, # statistical warmup before convergence detection activates ) opt.run() opt.best_snapshot # -> PolicySnapshot: best weights + EvalMetrics + HyperparamSet Loop states: ACTIVE → COOLING → DORMANT → watchdog shutdown or policy spawn . Every non-improving eval counts toward COOLING / DORMANT (on-policy and off-policy alike), and the eval interval backs off while the score is flat - set backoff_factor=1.0 to evaluate every window. rollback_on_degradation=True restores the best checkpoint when a degradation is confirmed over min_consecutive_degradations evals (on-policy agents only). On shutdown the loop restores best-known weights, not the final checkpoint. See Concepts for why, and Loop controller reference for the full constructor and degradation-handling details. Avoiding unicorn checkpoints By default, "best" means the single episode with the highest raw primary_score . That's fine most of the time, but it has a failure mode worth knowing about: a lucky episode during early, high-entropy exploration - reward concentrated on one favorable step rather than earned consistently - can score higher than anything that follows, even once the policy is genuinely, durably better. That lucky episode ("unicorn") then becomes a permanent, unbeatable "best," because nothing revisits whether it was ever a reliable measurement in the first place. Two opt-in RLOptimizer parameters address this: opt = RLOptimizer( agent=agent, pipeline=pipeline, criteria_mode="auto", # or "manual", or "both" checkpoint_confirm_window=3, # consecutive evals needed to corroborate ) criteria_mode="auto" - zero extra code. tensor-optix measures how concentrated vs. distributed each episode's reward was (using the shape of the reward stream every episode already has), and compares that shape against this run's own history - so it never penalizes domains where every legitimate win is naturally concentrated (e.g. a sparse terminal bonus in a landing task). criteria_mode="manual" - for when you know exactly what "good" means for your task and it's more than one number. Override criteria() on your BaseEvaluator subclass: python class RobotTaskEvaluator(TFEvaluator): def criteria(self, episode_data, train_diagnostics) -> dict: info = episode_data.infos[-1] return { "reached_goal": 1.0 if info.get("success") else 0.0, "avoided_collision": 0.0 if info.get("collided") else 1.0, "within_energy_budget": min(1.0, info.get("energy_left", 0) / 10.0), } A policy that only satisfies one of these three should not out-rank one that satisfies all three, even if its raw reward happened to be higher. - criteria_mode="both" combines the two (geometric mean). checkpoint_confirmation (implicitly enabled whenever criteria_mode isn't "none" ) is a separate, complementary layer: it doesn't judge whether an improvement is narrow or broad (that's what criteria_mode is for) - it just requires enough evidence that an improvement isn't purely this run's own noise, either because the measured noise is already small or because checkpoint_confirm_window consecutive evals corroborate it. Both are opt-in and default to the pre-existing behavior ( criteria_mode="none" ) so upgrading tensor-optix never silently changes what gets checkpointed in an existing project. See BaseEvaluator and LoopController for the full mechanism and config surface. Validation pipelines When val_pipeline is set, primary_score becomes the validation score and EvalMetrics.generalization_gap (train − val) becomes available. The validation pipeline's act() calls populate the agent's on-policy rollout cache; LoopController calls agent.reset_cache() (if the agent defines it) immediately after scoring validation, so that data is never accidentally consumed by the next training learn() call. Callbacks from tensor_optix.callbacks import RichDashboardCallback, WandbCallback, TensorBoardCallback opt.add_callback(RichDashboardCallback()) # Rich live terminal panel opt.add_callback(WandbCallback(project="run")) opt.add_callback(TensorBoardCallback(log_dir="./tb")) Custom callbacks subclass LoopCallback and override any of on_loop_start , on_loop_stop , on_episode_end , on_improvement , on_plateau , on_dormant , on_degradation , on_hyperparam_update . See Logging and dashboards and the Callbacks reference . Verbose mode verbose=True (optionally with verbose_log_file=... ) prints a per-eval breakdown: raw/smoothed/best score, trend slope vs. adaptive floor, loop state, and any hyperparameter changes from the active optimizer - useful when tuning convergence thresholds for a new environment.
docs.title: Train an RL agent

docs.text: Run trial-level search Online optimizers (SPSA, etc. - see Tune hyperparameters online ) adapt hyperparameters within one training run. They're good at tracking a non-stationary score landscape but can't efficiently explore the full hyperparameter space from a cold start. TrialOrchestrator runs N independent short trials via Optuna's TPE (Tree-structured Parzen Estimator) sampler before the main run, then identifies the best configuration. Standalone usage from tensor_optix import TrialOrchestrator orch = TrialOrchestrator( agent_factory=make_agent, pipeline_factory=make_pipeline, param_space={ "learning_rate": ("log_float", 1e-4, 3e-3), "clip_ratio": ("float", 0.1, 0.3), "batch_size": ("int", 32, 512), }, n_trials=20, trial_steps=50_000, ) best_params, best_score = orch.run() param_space entries are sampling specs: Spec Meaning ("float", lo, hi) uniform float ("log_float", lo, hi) log-uniform float - use for learning rates ("int", lo, hi) uniform int ("log_int", lo, hi) log-uniform int ("categorical", v1, v2, ...) one of the listed values A MedianPruner terminates clearly bad trials early (after a warmup phase, any trial whose intermediate score falls below the median of trials at the same step is killed) - this is successive-halving without needing to pre-commit to a fixed budget split. Composing with RLOptimizer RLOptimizer can run trial search automatically as a precursor to the main run - pass factories instead of constructed objects: optimizer = RLOptimizer( agent_factory=lambda params: MyAgent(params), pipeline_factory=lambda: MyPipeline(), param_space={ "learning_rate": ("log_float", 1e-4, 3e-3), "clip_ratio": ("float", 0.1, 0.3), }, n_trials=20, trial_steps_fraction=0.15, # 15% of max_steps per trial ) optimizer.run() # trial search runs first, then full training with best params run() performs trial search, builds the main agent via agent_factory(best_params) , warm-starts it from the best trial's saved weights (so trial compute isn't wasted on a cold re-init), deletes all trial checkpoint directories, and then runs the full loop with SPSA online adaptation on top of the trial-discovered configuration. Use trial_agent_factory instead of (or in addition to) agent_factory if trial-run agent construction needs to differ from the main-run construction (e.g. skip callback registration during trials). Reference Full constructor and method signatures: Trial search reference .

docs.text: API Reference This section documents every public class and function in tensor-optix, organized by module. Docstrings are reproduced verbatim from source. core - the framework-agnostic abstractions ( BaseAgent , BasePipeline , BaseEvaluator , BaseOptimizer , LoopController / LoopCallback ) plus shared utilities (checkpointing, normalizers, replay buffers, regime detection, ensembles). Top-level API - RLOptimizer and the simplified Optimizer wrapper. make_agent - the auto-selection factory. Algorithms - the 15 built-in agents across PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX/Flax. Pipelines - BatchPipeline , LivePipeline , VectorBatchPipeline . Multi-agent - PettingZoo Parallel/AEC pipelines, SeatEnvView , MultiAgentRunner (per-seat convergence, checkpoints, tuning), self-play ( SelfPlayConfig , SelfPlayPipeline ). Encoders - observation encoders for image and Dict observation spaces. Optimizers - SPSA, Momentum, Backoff, PBT, Adaptive (hyperparameter tuning). Callbacks - Rich dashboard, Weights & Biases, TensorBoard, AsyncCallbackAdapter . Distributed - IMPALA-style async actor-learner with V-trace. Trial search - TrialOrchestrator (Optuna-based). Config / CLI - YAML config loading and the tensor-optix CLI. ml_core - BaseMLModel , Trainer , metrics, LR schedules, transfer learning. ML mode (legacy) - training arbitrary nn.Module s with the RL loop. Learning-to-Learn Engine - ledger, concurrent scheduler, selection, nanonets, strategy discovery, live runtime. Exploration - RNDPipeline (Random Network Distillation). Neuroevo - the dynamic-topology policy subsystem.

ML mode (legacy) - training arbitrary nn.Module s with the RL loop. Learning-to-Learn Engine - ledger, concurrent scheduler, selection, nanonets, strategy discovery, live runtime. Exploration - RNDPipeline (Random Network Distillation). Neuroevo - the dynamic-topology policy subsystem.

docs.text: tensor_optix.algorithms - Algorithms All agents implement BaseAgent and are interchangeable with RLOptimizer . Each is built via make_agent() with sensible defaults, or constructed manually for custom network architectures. PyTorch Agent Algorithm Action Space TorchPPOAgent PPO + GAE-λ Discrete TorchGaussianPPOAgent PPO Continuous TorchRecurrentPPOAgent PPO + GRU/LSTM hidden state Discrete TorchDQNAgent DQN + PER + n-step returns Discrete TorchRainbowDQNAgent Rainbow DQN (NoisyNet, distributional, PER, n-step, dueling, double) Discrete TorchSACAgent SAC, twin Q-critics, automatic entropy tuning Continuous TorchTD3Agent TD3, twin-delayed deterministic policy gradient Continuous TensorFlow TFPPOAgent , TFGaussianPPOAgent , TFDQNAgent , TFSACAgent , TFTDDAgent (TD3) - same algorithmic coverage as the PyTorch agents for the standard (non-Rainbow, non-recurrent) cases. JAX / Flax FlaxPPOAgent - PPO via flax.nnx . Base adapters Each framework has a thin *Agent / *Evaluator pair that the algorithm-specific classes build on: TorchAgent / TorchEvaluator - base PyTorch agent (generic policy-gradient learn() , A2C advantage baseline when values are present, REINFORCE fallback otherwise) and the default evaluator (mean return of the episodes that completed in the window - split per env for VectorBatchPipeline windows - falling back to mean per-step reward when no episode completes in the window). TFAgent / TFEvaluator - same role for TensorFlow, using tf.GradientTape . FlaxAgent / FlaxEvaluator - same role for Flax NNX models. Weights are serialized via flax.nnx.to_pure_dict(nnx.state(model)) (a plain nested dict of numpy arrays) rather than raw pickling, since JAX arrays aren't reliably pickle-safe across JAX/XLA versions. Subclass the relevant base adapter and override learn() to wrap a custom architecture in algorithm-specific update logic (PPO clipping, SAC entropy tuning, DQN target updates, etc.) without reimplementing act() / save_weights() / load_weights() from scratch. Notable implementation details TorchRainbowDQNAgent combines all six Rainbow improvements: NoisyLinear layers (see NoisyLinear ) replace ε-greedy exploration, a distributional (categorical) value head, PrioritizedReplayBuffer , n-step returns, dueling architecture, and double-DQN target computation. TorchRecurrentPPOAgent carries GRU/LSTM hidden state across act() calls, caches the pre-step hidden state of every step, and trains with truncated BPTT ( bptt_len ), analogous to neuroevo's RecurrentGraphAgent . BatchPipeline calls its reset_hidden() at every episode boundary; when a window ends mid-episode the value target is bootstrapped from the critic on final_obs using the live hidden state. It holds a single hidden state, so use it with BatchPipeline , not VectorBatchPipeline . TorchTD3Agent implements the standard TD3 fixes: target policy smoothing ( target_noise / target_noise_clip ), delayed policy updates ( policy_delay ), and twin critics with the min-of-two target - its _soft_update does Polyak averaging θ_target ← τ·θ_source + (1−τ)·θ_target ; critic targets are updated every gradient step, the actor target only on the delayed steps where the actor itself is updated. act() is deterministic by default; set the exploration_noise hyperparameter (e.g. 0.1 , as in the TD3 paper) to add clipped Gaussian noise to collected actions, and set it back to 0 for evaluation/deployment. The same applies to TFTDDAgent . export_onnx is implemented on all Torch agents (continuous agents apply tanh internally and export actions clipped to (-1, 1) - rescale at deployment) - see Export to ONNX . Parallel envs : every built-in agent except TorchRecurrentPPOAgent accepts VectorBatchPipeline windows - PPO agents run GAE per env, off-policy agents build replay transitions per env (see Pipelines ). Replay transitions : off-policy agents store (s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1}, done_t) for consecutive steps inside a window; the last step of each env in a window has no in-window successor and is not stored. done is terminated OR truncated . is_on_policy : True for the PPO family (default), False for DQN/Rainbow/SAC/TD3 - see BaseAgent for why this matters to rollback. Auto-selection See make_agent for the factory that builds any of these with default networks from just a Gymnasium environment.

docs.text: tensor_optix.callbacks RichDashboardCallback class RichDashboardCallback(LoopCallback): """ Live terminal dashboard using the ``rich`` library. Architecture: LoopCallback hooks write lightweight event dicts into a thread-safe deque and return immediately (~μs overhead). A single daemon background thread owns the rich.Live context, reads from the deque, updates display state, and re-renders the panel at refresh_per_second Hz. Latency guarantee: on_episode_end appends a dict to a collections.deque and returns - O(1), lock-free on CPython (GIL-protected). No rendering, I/O, or allocation beyond the event dict happens in the hot path. Measured overhead is < 0.05 ms per episode on all tested hardware. Requires: pip install rich Parameters ---------- title : str - Header label shown in the panel. history : int - Number of recent episode scores to display. refresh_per_second : int - Redraw rate (default 4 - avoids flicker). show_hyperparams : bool - Whether to display the hyperparameter column. transient : bool - If True, dashboard is erased when training stops. Default False. """ def __init__( self, title="tensor-optix", history=50, refresh_per_second=4, show_hyperparams=True, transient=False, ): ... WandbCallback class WandbCallback(LoopCallback): """ Logs tensor-optix loop events to Weights & Biases. Requires: pip install wandb Signal groups logged every eval: score/primary, score/best, score/at_degradation metrics/* - full EvalMetrics.metrics breakdown hyperparams/* - on improvement and every SPSA update spsa/step_magnitude - L2 norm of relative per-param SPSA changes: ||Δx / |x_old|||₂ across all tuned params events/improvement, events/plateau, events/convergence, events/degradation Args: project, name, config, tags, group, resume - forwarded to wandb.init(). **init_kwargs - any additional kwargs forwarded to wandb.init(). """ def __init__( self, project=None, name=None, config=None, tags=None, group=None, resume=None, **init_kwargs, ): ... spsa/step_magnitude is only logged when the accumulated squared step is positive - it's a measure of SPSA aggression: large during plateau (probe scale widens), small during active improvement (probe scale shrinks). TensorBoardCallback class TensorBoardCallback(LoopCallback): """ Logs tensor-optix loop events to TensorBoard via SummaryWriter. Requires: pip install torch (SummaryWriter ships with torch.utils.tensorboard) or: pip install tensor-optix[tensorboard] Logs the same signal groups as WandbCallback (score/*, metrics/*, hyperparams/*, spsa/step_magnitude, events/*) using TensorBoard's '/' scalar-tag grouping convention. Args: log_dir: Directory for event files. Default ./runs/tensor_optix. comment: Suffix appended to log_dir when log_dir is not set. flush_secs: How often (seconds) the writer flushes to disk. Default 10. **writer_kwargs: forwarded to SummaryWriter(). """ def __init__(self, log_dir=None, comment="", flush_secs=10, **writer_kwargs): ... AsyncCallbackAdapter tensor_optix.core.async_callback class AsyncCallbackAdapter(LoopCallback): """ Wraps `inner` so its hooks run on a background thread via a bounded queue, never on the training thread. Overflow policy: when the queue is full, the OLDEST pending event is dropped to make room for the newest one. Dropped events are counted. """ def __init__(self, inner: LoopCallback, maxsize: int = 256): ... @property def dropped_count(self) -> int: ... @property def pending_count(self) -> int: ... def close(self, timeout: Optional[float] = None) -> None: """Stop the background thread once training is done.""" LoopController fires callbacks synchronously on the training thread, so a slow callback (GUI update, network I/O) stalls training. Wrap such a callback in AsyncCallbackAdapter to decouple it. Only use it for callbacks that are safe to run on another thread and do not need to observe or influence training synchronously - a wrapped callback cannot, for example, resume the loop at DORMANT . ExperimentLedgerCallback Records a run into the experiment ledger - documented with the ledger in Learning-to-Learn reference . See Logging and dashboards for usage and writing your own LoopCallback . Step numbering WandbCallback and TensorBoardCallback log hyperparameter updates at the episode currently being evaluated. Within one evaluated episode the loop fires on_improvement / on_plateau / on_degradation , then on_hyperparam_update , then on_episode_end ; steps are kept monotonic across those hooks so Weights & Biases does not drop the hyperparameter entries.

docs.text: tensor_optix.config and the CLI TrainConfig @dataclass class TrainConfig: """Fully-specified training configuration.""" env: str algorithm: str framework: str = "torch" deterministic: bool = False hidden_sizes: List[int] = field(default_factory=lambda: [256, 256]) pipeline: str = "BatchPipeline" window_size: int = 2048 seed: int = 0 agent: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict) optimizer: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict) Required keys: env (Gymnasium env ID), algorithm (one of TorchPPOAgent , TorchSACAgent , TorchTD3Agent , TorchDQNAgent , TorchGaussianPPOAgent , TorchRecurrentPPOAgent , TFPPOAgent , TFSACAgent , TFTDDAgent , TFDQNAgent , TFGaussianPPOAgent ). framework is inferred from the algorithm name prefix when omitted. Functions def load_config(path: str, overrides: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> TrainConfig: """ Load a YAML config file and apply optional CLI override strings. overrides: List of "key=value" strings. Dotted keys address nested dicts: "agent.learning_rate=1e-3". Values are YAML-parsed so true, 1e-3, [64,64] all work. Raises FileNotFoundError, KeyError (missing required key), or ValueError (malformed override / unrecognised algorithm). """ def apply_overrides(config_dict: dict, overrides: List[str]) -> dict: """ Apply a list of "dotted.key=value" overrides to a config dict. Returns a new dict (does not mutate the input). >>> apply_overrides({"agent": {"lr": 1e-4}}, ["agent.lr=1e-3", "seed=42"]) {'agent': {'lr': 0.001}, 'seed': 42} """ def config_to_dict(cfg: TrainConfig) -> dict: """Serialise a TrainConfig back to a plain dict (YAML-round-trippable).""" def build_agent_from_config(cfg: TrainConfig): """ Build the agent and its HyperparamSet from a TrainConfig. Uses make_agent() for automatic network construction, routed to the algorithm family named by cfg.algorithm (PPO / DQN / SAC / TD3). Returns (agent, hyperparams). Raises ValueError when the factory cannot build exactly cfg.algorithm for this env/framework (see "Algorithm resolution" below). """ def build_pipeline_from_config(cfg: TrainConfig): """ Build the pipeline from a TrainConfig. "BatchPipeline" wraps gym.make(cfg.env) with cfg.window_size. "LivePipeline" raises ValueError for a plain Gymnasium env: it needs a data source exposing stream(), which only Python code can provide. """ def build_optimizer_from_config(cfg: TrainConfig, agent, pipeline): """ Build an RLOptimizer from a TrainConfig + already-constructed components. Only passes kwargs that are actually present in cfg.optimizer - raises ValueError on unrecognised keys rather than silently ignoring typos. """ Precedence order: defaults < config file < CLI overrides . Algorithm resolution algorithm is honoured, not just validated. The class name selects the make_agent() family and the built agent's class must match it exactly, otherwise build_agent_from_config() raises ValueError naming what it could build: algorithm Works with Notes TorchPPOAgent / TFPPOAgent Discrete actions TorchGaussianPPOAgent / TFGaussianPPOAgent Continuous (Box) actions TorchDQNAgent Discrete actions TorchSACAgent / TFSACAgent Continuous actions TorchTD3Agent / TFTDDAgent Continuous actions deterministic: true is implied TFDQNAgent , TorchRecurrentPPOAgent - accepted by validate , but make_agent() has no builder for them: train exits with a build error. Construct these agents in Python. A mismatch such as algorithm: TorchPPOAgent on a continuous-action env is an error rather than a silent substitution. CLI Registered as the tensor-optix console script: tensor-optix train config.yaml [key=value ...] tensor-optix validate config.yaml [key=value ...] train loads the config, seeds random / numpy / torch (and CUDA, if available; TensorFlow too when it is already imported) from cfg.seed , builds agent/pipeline/optimizer via the functions above, and calls optimizer.run() . Exits 1 with a printed error on a config or build failure rather than a raw traceback. validate parses and validates the config (same error handling) without building or running anything - prints the resolved env , algorithm , framework , seed , and any agent / optimizer sub-dicts. Exits 0 on success, 1 on error - suitable for a CI gate. See Configure via YAML / CLI for the full schema and a worked example.

docs.text: tensor_optix.distributed IMPALA-style asynchronous actor-learner training with V-trace off-policy correction (Espeholt et al. 2018, arXiv:1802.01561 ). AsyncActorLearner class AsyncActorLearner: """ IMPALA-style async actor-learner for PyTorch discrete policies. N actor processes run environment episodes in parallel, each using the current policy weights read directly from shared memory (via torch.Tensor.share_memory_()). A single learner (main process) dequeues trajectories, applies V-trace IS correction, and performs gradient updates. Weight updates are immediately visible to all actors - no explicit weight broadcast queue, no serialization overhead. Platform note: 'fork' is used automatically on Linux (no pickling required), 'spawn' on Windows/macOS (env_factory must be picklable - a module-level function or functools.partial, not a lambda with a non-picklable closure). Parameters ---------- actor nn.Module - policy network (obs → logits over actions) critic nn.Module - value network (obs → scalar) optimizer torch.optim.Optimizer - over all actor+critic parameters env_factory Callable → gym.Env - called once per actor process. n_actors int - parallel actor processes (default 4) trajectory_len int - environment steps per trajectory batch (default 64) max_queue_size int - max pending trajectories (0 = 8 × n_actors) gamma float - discount factor rho_bar float - V-trace IS weight clip ρ̄ (default 1.0) c_bar float - V-trace trace clip c̄ (default 1.0) entropy_coef float - entropy bonus coefficient vf_coef float - value function loss coefficient max_grad_norm float - gradient norm clipping threshold seed int - base random seed; actor i uses seed + i×7919 """ def run(self, max_steps: int) -> dict: """ Launch actor processes and run the learner loop. Blocks until max_steps total environment steps have been collected across all actors, then signals all actors to stop and waits for them to exit. Returns ------- dict with: total_steps, total_updates, steps_per_second, elapsed Raises ------ RuntimeError if every actor process exits before max_steps is reached (e.g. env_factory raises in the workers) - the learner fails loudly instead of waiting forever for trajectories. """ compute_vtrace_targets def compute_vtrace_targets( rewards, # shape [T] per-step rewards values, # shape [T+1] V(s_t) for t=0..T; values[T] is bootstrap behaviour_log_probs, # shape [T] log π_μ(a_t|s_t) recorded by the actor current_log_probs, # shape [T] log π_θ(a_t|s_t) from current learner policy dones, # shape [T] bool - True when episode ended at step t gamma: float, rho_bar: float = 1.0, c_bar: float = 1.0, ): """ Compute V-trace targets and policy-gradient advantages. IS ratio: ρ_t = π_θ(a_t|s_t) / π_μ(a_t|s_t) Clipped: ρ̄_t = min(ρ̄, ρ_t) c̄_t = min(c̄, ρ_t) V-trace target (backward recursion): δ_t = ρ̄_t · (r_t + γ·V(s_{t+1})·(1−done_t) − V(s_t)) v_T = V(s_T) v_t = V(s_t) + δ_t + γ·c̄_t·(v_{t+1} − V(s_{t+1})) Policy-gradient advantage: A_t = ρ̄_t · (r_t + γ·v_{t+1}·(1−done_t) − V(s_t)) Setting ρ̄ = c̄ = 1 and μ = θ (on-policy) recovers standard GAE with λ = c̄. Returns ------- vs shape [T] V-trace targets for the value regression loss advantages shape [T] IS-corrected policy-gradient advantages """ See Distributed training (IMPALA + V-trace) for usage guidance.

docs.text: class AsyncActorLearner: """ IMPALA-style async actor-learner for PyTorch discrete policies. N actor processes run environment episodes in parallel, each using the current policy weights read directly from shared memory (via torch.Tensor.share_memory_()). A single learner (main process) dequeues trajectories, applies V-trace IS correction, and performs gradient updates. Weight updates are immediately visible to all actors - no explicit weight broadcast queue, no serialization overhead. Platform note: 'fork' is used automatically on Linux (no pickling required), 'spawn' on Windows/macOS (env_factory must be picklable - a module-level function or functools.partial, not a lambda with a non-picklable closure). Parameters ---------- actor nn.Module - policy network (obs → logits over actions) critic nn.Module - value network (obs → scalar) optimizer torch.optim.Optimizer - over all actor+critic parameters env_factory Callable → gym.Env - called once per actor process. n_actors int - parallel actor processes (default 4) trajectory_len int - environment steps per trajectory batch (default 64) max_queue_size int - max pending trajectories (0 = 8 × n_actors) gamma float - discount factor rho_bar float - V-trace IS weight clip ρ̄ (default 1.0) c_bar float - V-trace trace clip c̄ (default 1.0) entropy_coef float - entropy bonus coefficient vf_coef float - value function loss coefficient max_grad_norm float - gradient norm clipping threshold seed int - base random seed; actor i uses seed + i×7919 """ def run(self, max_steps: int) -> dict: """ Launch actor processes and run the learner loop. Blocks until max_steps total environment steps have been collected across all actors, then signals all actors to stop and waits for them to exit. Returns ------- dict with: total_steps, total_updates, steps_per_second, elapsed Raises ------ RuntimeError if every actor process exits before max_steps is reached (e.g. env_factory raises in the workers) - the learner fails loudly instead of waiting forever for trajectories. """

docs.text: tensor_optix.encoders Observation encoders that let make_agent() build agents for non-flat observation spaces. Every network make_agent() constructs sits on top of an encoder mapping a raw observation to a flat feature vector. Observation space Encoder Output width flat 1-D Box identity (pass-through - network dimensions identical to a hand-built MLP) shape[0] image Box (H, W, C) , C ∈ {1, 3, 4} CNN: Nature-DQN stack for min(H, W) ≥ 36 , a smaller 3×3 stack down to 12 feature_dim (256) Dict of the above one sub-encoder per key, outputs concatenated sum of the parts Anything else ( MultiDiscrete , Tuple , MultiBinary , nested Dict , other Box ranks) raises NotImplementedError - build the agent manually. Torch from tensor_optix.encoders import ( EncodedHead, build_torch_encoder, encoder_output_dim, is_flat_box, is_image_box, ) def build_torch_encoder(space, feature_dim: int = 256) -> nn.Module: """ Build a fresh nn.Module mapping an observation from `space` to a flat [batch, encoder_output_dim(space, feature_dim)] feature tensor. Each call returns an independently-initialised module - actor and critics never share encoder weights. """ def encoder_output_dim(space, feature_dim: int = 256) -> int: """The flat width build_torch_encoder() will produce, without building it.""" class EncodedHead(nn.Module): """encoder followed by head; exposes .encoder and .head separately.""" def __init__(self, encoder, head): ... TensorFlow from tensor_optix.encoders.obs_encoder_tf import build_tf_encoder def build_tf_encoder(space, feature_dim: int = 256, input_name: str = None): ... Same architecture constants as the Torch builder. How agents use encoders PPO family (on-policy). The encoder is part of the actor/critic and trains end-to-end through the usual minibatch updates. SAC / TD3. Observations are encoded with the actor's encoder before entering the replay buffer, so the buffer always stores flat float32 vectors and the critics only ever see encoded features. The encoding happens once at collection time; replayed Q-loss gradients do not flow back into the encoder. DQN / Rainbow. A single Q-network serves both act() and the Bellman update, so the buffer stores the raw (possibly Dict ) observation and the network's own EncodedHead runs on every call - trained end-to-end. Helpers for batching flat/image/ Dict observations uniformly live in tensor_optix.core.obs_utils ( to_batch_numpy , to_torch_batch , to_tf_batch , batch_index ).

docs.text: tensor_optix.exploration.rnd Random Network Distillation (RND) exploration bonus. RND adds an intrinsic reward signal to any pipeline without modifying any agent. Two small networks - a frozen random target and a trained predictor - both map observations to a fixed embedding space. Novel states produce high prediction error (high intrinsic reward). Visited states are fitted well (low bonus). Math: r_int(s) = ||f_θ(s) - g(s)||² (g frozen, f_θ trained) r_total = r_ext + η · r_int / σ(r_int) (intrinsic normalized per episode) η is controlled by the loop via set_eta(): ACTIVE → η = η_base (default exploration level) COOLING → η *= 1.5 (stuck - push exploration harder) DORMANT → η = 0 (converged - stop injecting noise) improvement → η *= 0.9 (getting better - reduce exploration) RNDPipeline wraps any BasePipeline. It intercepts EpisodeData after each episode and injects the intrinsic bonus into episode_data.rewards before the agent sees them. The predictor network is trained on the current batch each episode. Framework: pure numpy + a minimal two-layer MLP. No TF or Torch dependency. The target network is random and fixed; the predictor is updated via SGD. RNDPipeline class RNDPipeline(BasePipeline): """ Wraps any BasePipeline and injects RND intrinsic rewards into each episode. After each episode, before returning EpisodeData: 1. Compute r_int(s) = ||predictor(s) - target(s)||² for each step 2. Normalize r_int by its running std 3. Inject: rewards[t] += eta * r_int[t] 4. Train predictor on current batch observations The loop controls eta via set_eta() at state transitions. Args: pipeline: The wrapped pipeline (any BasePipeline). obs_dim: Observation dimension (flattened). embedding_dim: RND embedding size. Default 64 - larger = slower but richer. eta: Initial intrinsic reward scale. Default 0.1. predictor_lr: SGD learning rate for the predictor. Default 1e-3. norm_eps: Small constant for std normalization. Default 1e-8. """ def __init__( self, pipeline: BasePipeline, obs_dim: int, embedding_dim: int = 64, eta: float = 0.1, predictor_lr: float = 1e-3, norm_eps: float = 1e-8, ): ... def set_eta(self, eta: float) -> None: """Called by LoopController at state transitions to adjust exploration scale.""" # BasePipeline interface: setup, teardown, episodes, is_live - all delegate # to the wrapped pipeline, with episodes() injecting the intrinsic bonus. # Any other attribute access (e.g. set_agent, n_steps) proxies through # to the wrapped pipeline via __getattr__. Running stats for intrinsic-reward normalization use Welford's online algorithm (mean and variance updated incrementally, one r_int value at a time). See Add exploration bonuses (RND) for usage with RLOptimizer .
docs.title: Exploration (RND)

docs.text: tensor_optix.factory - make_agent The action space type is a mathematical property that *determines* the valid policy parameterisation. This factory makes that mapping explicit and enforces it: Discrete(n) → TorchPPOAgent / TFPPOAgent (categorical π(a|s) = softmax(logits)) Box(shape) → TorchSACAgent / TFSACAgent [default] TorchTD3Agent / TFTDDAgent [deterministic=True] MultiDiscrete → NotImplementedError Dict / Tuple → NotImplementedError When neuroevo=True the policy is a NeuronGraph wrapped in GraphAgent (PPO-based). The algorithm argument in that case influences hyperparameter defaults only. make_agent def make_agent( algorithm_or_env, env=None, algorithm: Optional[str] = None, framework: str = "torch", deterministic: bool = False, hidden_sizes: Tuple[int, ...] = (256, 256), hyperparams: Optional[HyperparamSet] = None, device: str = "auto", # Neuroevo options neuroevo: bool = False, neuroevo_mode: str = "policy", # "policy" | "feature_extractor" graph_in: Optional[int] = None, graph_hidden: int = 8, graph_out: Optional[int] = None, hebbian_lr: float = 1e-3, hebbian_decay: float = 1e-4, grow_cooldown: int = 20, ): """ Inspect *env* and return a fully-constructed agent with default networks. Parameters ---------- env: A Gymnasium environment (or any object with ``.observation_space`` and ``.action_space`` attributes). framework: ``"torch"`` (default) or ``"tf"``. deterministic: Only relevant for continuous (Box) action spaces. When ``True`` returns TD3 (deterministic policy); when ``False`` returns SAC (stochastic policy with entropy regularisation). hidden_sizes: Hidden layer widths for all networks. Default: ``(256, 256)``. hyperparams: Optional HyperparamSet override. When ``None``, sensible defaults for the selected algorithm are used. device: ``"auto"``, ``"cpu"``, or ``"cuda"``. Passed to the agent; ignored for the TF backend (TF manages device placement automatically). Returns ------- BaseAgent - a fully constructed, ready-to-train agent instance. Raises ------ NotImplementedError When the action space type has no supported algorithm, or when the observation space is not a flat 1-D Box. """ Positional overloading agent = make_agent(env) # algorithm inferred from action space agent = make_agent("SAC", env) # algorithm explicit Routing table Action space algorithm= Result Discrete(n) (none) TorchPPOAgent / TFPPOAgent Discrete(n) "DQN" TorchDQNAgent Discrete(n) "RAINBOW" TorchRainbowDQNAgent Box(shape) , 1-D (none), deterministic=False TorchSACAgent / TFSACAgent Box(shape) , 1-D deterministic=True or "TD3" TorchTD3Agent / TFTDDAgent MultiDiscrete - NotImplementedError - no single correct factored-policy parameterisation Dict / Tuple - NotImplementedError - requires a custom policy architecture MultiBinary - NotImplementedError - requires a multi-label Bernoulli policy Observation spaces: the standard (non-neuroevo) path accepts a flat 1-D Box , an image Box of shape (H, W, C) with C ∈ {1, 3, 4} (CNN encoder), or a Dict of those (per-key encoders, concatenated) - see Encoders . Discrete , MultiDiscrete , MultiBinary , Tuple , nested Dict and other Box ranks raise NotImplementedError ; for PettingZoo seats with Discrete observations use SeatEnvView . The neuroevo path requires a flat 1-D Box . Neuroevo path When neuroevo=True : neuroevo_mode="policy" (default) - builds a NeuronGraph with graph_in input neurons (default min(obs_dim, 16) ), graph_hidden TrainableGRUNeuron s, and graph_out output neurons (default act_dim + 1 , last is the value head), fully connected input→hidden→output with weight 0.1 , dale_mode="softplus" . Wraps it in GraphAgent . Attaches agent._neuroevo_callbacks = [HebbianHook(...), TopologyController(...)] , which Optimizer / Optimizer -style wiring picks up automatically. neuroevo_mode="feature_extractor" - builds a smaller graph (orthogonal projection obs_dim → graph_in , TrainableGRUNeuron "sensory" layer, TrainableLSTMNeuron "memory" layer, tanh output layer) whose output is concatenated with the raw observation before a TorchSACAgent 's actor/critic networks. Attaches _neuroevo_callbacks = [TopologyController, HebbianHook, NeuromodulatorSignal] . Default hyperparameters by algorithm Algorithm Defaults PPO learning_rate=3e-4, clip_ratio=0.2, entropy_coef=0.01, vf_coef=0.5, gamma=0.99, gae_lambda=0.95, n_epochs=10, minibatch_size=64, max_grad_norm=0.5 DQN learning_rate=1e-3, gamma=0.99, epsilon=1.0→0.05 (decay 0.995), batch_size=64, target_update_freq=10, replay_capacity=10_000 Rainbow learning_rate=6.25e-5, gamma=0.99, batch_size=32, target_update_freq=200, replay_capacity=100_000, per_alpha=0.5, per_beta=0.4, n_step=3, v_min=0, v_max=500, n_atoms=51 SAC learning_rate=3e-4, gamma=0.99, tau=0.005, batch_size=256, updates_per_step=1, replay_capacity=1_000_000 TD3 learning_rate=3e-4, gamma=0.99, tau=0.005, batch_size=256, policy_delay=2, target_noise=0.2, target_noise_clip=0.5 See Algorithms for the agent classes themselves. Rainbow value support make_agent("RAINBOW", env) defaults to a categorical support of [v_min=0, v_max=500] , which fits CartPole-like returns only (a warning is logged when the default is used). Returns outside the support are clamped, so pass hyperparams with v_min / v_max covering your env's discounted-return range for anything else.

docs.text: Learning-to-Learn Engine Six composable layers, each reading/writing the shared experiment ledger: 1. tensor_optix.ledger - ExperimentStore (SQLite-backed, idempotent, provenance-tracked) 2. tensor_optix.scheduler - ConcurrentTrialScheduler (real mp.Process worker isolation) 3. tensor_optix.selection - StrategySelector (non-learned baseline allocation) 4. tensor_optix.nanonets - NanonetsSelector (cross-task pooling, conservative abstention gate) 5. tensor_optix.strategy - typed grammar, StrategyTrialRunner, PromotionPolicy 6. tensor_optix.runtime - LiveAdaptiveRuntime (recommend-only observe/experiment/evaluate loop) No layer uses generative AI or executes arbitrary generated code. Strategy candidates are reconstructed only from a fixed OP_REGISTRY via keyword arguments matching each dataclass's declared fields -- never eval()/exec(). See the guide for narrative usage: ../guides/learning-to-learn.md 1. Attach it to any RLOptimizer / LoopController run to record that run in the ledger: the experiment row (with provenance: tensor-optix version, git revision, library versions, hostname), one event per loop hook, a progress update and an ArtifactRef (with a SHA-256 of the weights) per improvement. Terminal state is decided in on_loop_stop , which the loop fires from run() 's finally : How the run ended state evaluation_status returned normally COMPLETED PRELIMINARY an exception is propagating FAILED (with error_message ) INCONCLUSIVE KeyboardInterrupt CANCELLED INCONCLUSIVE So a crashed run is recorded as failed without any caller-side handling; calling mark_failed(exc) yourself afterwards is harmless (finalization is idempotent). Returns (best_params, best_score).""" @property def study(self) -> "optuna.Study": ... Workers never touch the Optuna Study or the ExperimentStore directly — they receive a plain sampled-params dict and report scores back over a queue; all ledger/study writes happen in the parent process. Failure handling: A worker that raises reports status="failed" ; that is a property of the trial, not of the infrastructure, so it is not retried - the trial is told to Optuna as FAIL and finalized FAILED in the ledger. A worker process that dies without reporting (OOM-kill, segfault, external kill) is detected by the parent on the next poll. It is treated as transient and re-dispatched with a new seed up to max_retries times, then finalized FAILED with the exit code in error_message . run() therefore always terminates, with or without trial_timeout_s . A trial exceeding trial_timeout_s is cancelled and finalized TIMED_OUT . 3. Abstention gate ( tensor_optix.nanonets.abstention ): MIN_TARGET_N = 2 def normalize_score(raw_score: float, solve_threshold: float) -> Optional[float]: """(raw_score - solve_threshold) / abs(solve_threshold). None if solve_threshold == 0.0. Plain division is unsafe across a sign boundary -- this signed-distance form is not.""" def normalize_scores(raw_scores: List[float], solve_threshold: Optional[float]) -> Optional[List[float]]: ... def passes_percentile_gate(source_scores: List[float], target_scores: List[float]) -> bool: """A source is eligible iff its median >= the target's own 95th percentile, both on NORMALIZED scores.""" def similarity_weight(*, source_algorithm: str, target_algorithm: str, source_n: int, target_n: int) -> float: """Algorithm-family match contributes full weight (mismatch halves it); extreme sample-size imbalance scales the weight down further.""" Pooling ( tensor_optix.nanonets.pooling.pool_estimates ) combines the target's own scores with gate-passed sources via inverse-variance + similarity weighting. The caller ( NanonetsSelector ) normalizes inputs the same way the gate does before pooling, then de-normalizes the pooled result back to the target's own raw units — pooling in raw, mixed-scale units was a real bug found and fixed via live validation; pooling must happen in the same comparable space the gate uses, not a different one. 5. Strategy discovery ( tensor_optix.strategy ) @dataclass(frozen=True) class StrategyOp: op_name: ClassVar[str] = "" def required_capabilities(self) -> Tuple[str, ...]: ... def supports(self, agent: BaseAgent) -> bool: ... def attach(self, agent: BaseAgent, **kwargs) -> Optional[LoopCallback]: """Returns None (never raises) if `agent` lacks a capability this op needs -- self-exclusion is the primary safety mechanism.""" OP_REGISTRY: Dict[str, Type[StrategyOp]] # the 7 concrete ops, nothing else reachable The 7 concrete ops — LearningRateTrendOp , CheckpointRollbackOp , ExplorationBoundsOp , OptimizationMethodChoiceOp , BudgetAllocationOp , ScheduleChangeOp , PolicyVariantSelectionOp — each a frozen dataclass with named, typed fields; see the guide for field-level detail on each. @dataclass(frozen=True) class StrategyCandidate: candidate_id: str # sha256 content hash, first 16 hex chars op_name: str op_version: int params: Dict[str, Any] grammar_schema_version: int = 1 @staticmethod def from_op(op: StrategyOp, op_version: int = 1) -> "StrategyCandidate": ... def to_op(self) -> StrategyOp: """Reconstructs via OP_REGISTRY[self.op_name](**self.params) only -- never eval()/exec(). Raises ValueError for an unknown op_name, TypeError for an unknown param key (dataclass construction itself enforces the closed field set).""" class StrategyTrialRunner: def __init__( self, *, agent_factory: Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], BaseAgent], pipeline_factory: Callable[[], BasePipeline], base_params: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, rloptimizer_kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, checkpoint_score_fn: Optional[Callable[[BaseAgent], float]] = None, trial_steps: int = 50_000, ledger_store: Optional[ExperimentStore] = None, task_env: str = "", algorithm: str = "", framework: str = "torch", solve_threshold: Optional[float] = None, trial_timeout_s: Optional[float] = None, poll_interval_s: float = 0.5, ): ... def run_candidate(self, candidate: StrategyCandidate, *, seeds: List[int]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """For each seed, dispatches a PAIRED candidate + no-strategy- baseline mp.Process trial (same seed/task/budget). Returns a list of {seed, candidate_score, baseline_score, outcome_delta, candidate_experiment_id, baseline_experiment_id, candidate_status, baseline_status} dicts. Comparator ( tensor_optix.strategy.comparator ): MIN_EVALUATIONS = 3 def compare_candidate(store: ExperimentStore, candidate_id: str, task_env: str, *, margin: float = 0.0) -> StrategyComparison: """Gates on lo95(outcome_delta) > margin AND n_evaluations >= 3 -- the pessimistic CI bound, not the mean; hard floor on distinct seeds.""" def compare_against_approved(store: ExperimentStore, candidate_id: str, task_env: str, *, margin: float = 0.0) -> StrategyComparison: """As above, plus recomputes (never cached) each currently-approved strategy's own interval for the same task_env for a head-to-head check.""" In approval_mode="human" (default), human_reviewed can only become True via a prior, separate store.approve_strategy() call -- evaluate() never calls it. In approval_mode="auto", if the other five all pass, evaluate() calls approve_strategy() itself with reviewer="auto:PromotionPolicy" -- always traceable, never silent.""" @dataclass class PromotionVerdict: candidate_id: str approved: bool criteria: Dict[str, bool] rationale: str @dataclass class StrategyScope: task_envs: List[str] held_out_task_envs: List[str] algorithms: List[str] # exact strings tested, never "all" frameworks: List[str] budget_range_episodes: Tuple[int, int] n_seeds_per_task: int excluded_agents: List[str] confound_notes: str def record_candidate_scope(store, candidate, *, train_task_envs, held_out_task_envs, algorithms, frameworks, budget_range_episodes, n_seeds_per_task, excluded_agents=None, confound_notes="") -> StrategyScope: ... 6. Returns the experiment_id.""" def get_current_baseline_experiment_id(store, *, task_env, algorithm, study_id) -> Optional[str]: """Live lookup, never cached -- the deployed baseline can change at any time via promote.py's separate human-invoked path.""" def run_reevaluation(store, *, baseline_experiment_id, agent_factory, evaluator, task_env, algorithm, study_id, eval_episodes: int = 5) -> float: """Loads the baseline's weights into a fresh agent, runs a real, inference-only rollout (no learn() calls), records one deployed_baseline_eval row, returns the real score.""" class DeploymentObserver: def __init__(self, store, *, task_env, algorithm, study_id, scheduler: Optional[BackoffScheduler] = None): """Wraps BackoffScheduler (reused as-is, store-free, numpy-only -- not reimplemented) with a per-re-evaluation-cycle calling convention instead of per-episode.""" def observe(self, score: float) -> ObservationResult: ... def score_history(self, *, limit: int = 100) -> List[float]: ... def replay_history(self) -> None: """Reconstructs ledger-backed history and replays it through the scheduler -- makes Observer state durable across process restarts with zero new persistence code.""" @dataclass class ObservationResult: cycle: int score: float state: LoopState is_degrading: bool degradation_fired: bool best_score: Optional[float] def propose_and_run(store, *, agent_factory, pipeline_factory, task_env, algorithm, solve_threshold, source_task_envs, budget, trial_steps, seeds, trial_timeout_s: float = 180.0) -> List[Tuple[StrategyCandidate, List[Dict]]]: """Ranks a fixed, agent-appropriate shortlist of StrategyOps via NanonetsSelector.propose() (never invents a new op), runs whichever receive nonzero allocation through StrategyTrialRunner.""" def evaluate_and_recommend(store, candidate, trial_results, *, task_env, algorithm, trial_steps, seeds) -> PromotionVerdict: """Records scope, evaluates via a hardcoded approval_mode="human" PromotionPolicy, issues a durable recommendation event. Never calls approve_strategy.""" def issue_recommendation(store, candidate, verdict, *, experiment_id) -> None: """Appends one EventRecord(event_type="recommendation_issued") -- an auditable record, not a vanishing print line.""" @dataclass class RuntimeConfig: task_env: str = "CartPole-v1" algorithm: str = "PPO" study_id: str = "live_runtime_cartpole_v1" solve_threshold: float = 475.0 eval_episodes: int = 5 cycle_sleep_s: float = 1.0 research_cycle_every: int = 3 experiment_budget_trials: int = 2 experiment_trial_steps: int = 3_000 experiment_seeds: Tuple[int, ...] = (0, 1, 2) max_cycles: int = 6 source_task_envs: Tuple[str, ...] = () # Deliberately NO approval_mode field -- no parameter path reaches # PromotionPolicy's approval_mode from here. class LiveAdaptiveRuntime: def __init__(self, store: ExperimentStore, config: RuntimeConfig, *, agent_factory, pipeline_factory): ... def run(self) -> Tuple[List[ObservationResult], List[CycleRecommendation]]: """Single-threaded sequential loop, bounded by max_cycles. Each cycle: re-evaluate -> observe -> maybe propose_and_run -> evaluate_and_recommend -> sleep. Raises RuntimeError if no deployed baseline exists yet (call establish_baseline first).""" @dataclass class CycleRecommendation: cycle: int candidate_id: str op_name: str automatable_criteria_passed: bool rationale: str def promote_candidate_to_baseline( store: ExperimentStore, candidate_id: str, *, reviewer: str, task_env: str, algorithm: str, study_id: str, ) -> str: """The ONLY function that can change the deployed baseline. Raises ValueError unless the candidate's registry status is already APPROVED -- refuses to act on anything not already human-reviewed. Never imported by live_runtime.py, experiment_stage.py, observer.py, or baseline.py. Picks the candidate's best-scoring recorded weights_path and writes a new deployed_baseline ExperimentRecord.""" See the guide for the full end-to-end wiring: Learning-to-Learn Engine guide . Behaviour notes Method evidence. StrategySelector and NanonetsSelector count a ledger experiment as evidence for a method when config["sampler"] == method (trial-search runs) or config["op_name"] == method with is_baseline false (strategy-candidate runs). The live runtime's proposals over strategy ops therefore learn from earlier strategy trials. Untried methods are ranked last. CycleRecommendation.automatable_criteria_passed is True when every evidence-based criterion passed, ignoring human_reviewed (which the recommend-only loop never sets). Trial workers ( ConcurrentTrialScheduler , StrategyTrialRunner ) seed torch , numpy and random from the trial seed. CheckpointRollbackOp in a strategy trial rolls back to the run's current best checkpoint (it shares the run's CheckpointRegistry ). OptimizationMethodChoiceOp switches at most once per stall; after the run improves again, the next stall advances to the next entry of candidate_methods . run_reevaluation evaluates epsilon-greedy agents greedily ( epsilon = 0 ).

docs.text: Six composable layers, each reading/writing the shared experiment ledger: 1. tensor_optix.ledger - ExperimentStore (SQLite-backed, idempotent, provenance-tracked) 2. tensor_optix.scheduler - ConcurrentTrialScheduler (real mp.Process worker isolation) 3. tensor_optix.selection - StrategySelector (non-learned baseline allocation) 4. tensor_optix.nanonets - NanonetsSelector (cross-task pooling, conservative abstention gate) 5. tensor_optix.strategy - typed grammar, StrategyTrialRunner, PromotionPolicy 6. tensor_optix.runtime - LiveAdaptiveRuntime (recommend-only observe/experiment/evaluate loop) No layer uses generative AI or executes arbitrary generated code. Strategy candidates are reconstructed only from a fixed OP_REGISTRY via keyword arguments matching each dataclass's declared fields -- never eval()/exec(). See the guide for narrative usage: ../guides/learning-to-learn.md

Workers never touch the Optuna Study or the ExperimentStore directly — they receive a plain sampled-params dict and report scores back over a queue; all ledger/study writes happen in the parent process. Failure handling: A worker that raises reports status="failed" ; that is a property of the trial, not of the infrastructure, so it is not retried - the trial is told to Optuna as FAIL and finalized FAILED in the ledger. A worker process that dies without reporting (OOM-kill, segfault, external kill) is detected by the parent on the next poll. It is treated as transient and re-dispatched with a new seed up to max_retries times, then finalized FAILED with the exit code in error_message . run() therefore always terminates, with or without trial_timeout_s . A trial exceeding trial_timeout_s is cancelled and finalized TIMED_OUT .

docs.text: @dataclass class PooledEstimate: method: str pooled_mean: float pooled_interval: SmallNInterval sources_used: List[str] sources_gated_out: List[str] fallback_triggered: bool class NanonetsSelector: def __init__(self, store: ExperimentStore, *, source_task_envs: List[str]): """source_task_envs is always explicit -- never auto-discovered, so leave-one-task-out leakage discipline is enforced at the call site, not inferred.""" def task_features(self, task_env: str) -> TaskFeatures: ... def pooled_stats(self, *, task_env: str, method: str) -> PooledEstimate: ... def propose(self, *, task_env: str, methods: List[str], budget: int) -> SelectionDecision: """Falls back to StrategySelector.propose() if every method's pooled estimate triggers fallback_triggered.""" Abstention gate ( tensor_optix.nanonets.abstention ): MIN_TARGET_N = 2 def normalize_score(raw_score: float, solve_threshold: float) -> Optional[float]: """(raw_score - solve_threshold) / abs(solve_threshold). None if solve_threshold == 0.0. Plain division is unsafe across a sign boundary -- this signed-distance form is not.""" def normalize_scores(raw_scores: List[float], solve_threshold: Optional[float]) -> Optional[List[float]]: ... def passes_percentile_gate(source_scores: List[float], target_scores: List[float]) -> bool: """A source is eligible iff its median >= the target's own 95th percentile, both on NORMALIZED scores.""" def similarity_weight(*, source_algorithm: str, target_algorithm: str, source_n: int, target_n: int) -> float: """Algorithm-family match contributes full weight (mismatch halves it); extreme sample-size imbalance scales the weight down further.""" Pooling ( tensor_optix.nanonets.pooling.pool_estimates ) combines the target's own scores with gate-passed sources via inverse-variance + similarity weighting. The caller ( NanonetsSelector ) normalizes inputs the same way the gate does before pooling, then de-normalizes the pooled result back to the target's own raw units — pooling in raw, mixed-scale units was a real bug found and fixed via live validation; pooling must happen in the same comparable space the gate uses, not a different one.

Raises ValueError for an unknown op_name, TypeError for an unknown param key (dataclass construction itself enforces the closed field set).""" class StrategyTrialRunner: def __init__( self, *, agent_factory: Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], BaseAgent], pipeline_factory: Callable[[], BasePipeline], base_params: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, rloptimizer_kwargs: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None, checkpoint_score_fn: Optional[Callable[[BaseAgent], float]] = None, trial_steps: int = 50_000, ledger_store: Optional[ExperimentStore] = None, task_env: str = "", algorithm: str = "", framework: str = "torch", solve_threshold: Optional[float] = None, trial_timeout_s: Optional[float] = None, poll_interval_s: float = 0.5, ): ... def run_candidate(self, candidate: StrategyCandidate, *, seeds: List[int]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """For each seed, dispatches a PAIRED candidate + no-strategy- baseline mp.Process trial (same seed/task/budget). Returns a list of {seed, candidate_score, baseline_score, outcome_delta, candidate_experiment_id, baseline_experiment_id, candidate_status, baseline_status} dicts. Writes ExperimentRecords and one StrategyEvaluationRecord per seed if a ledger_store is supplied.""" Comparator ( tensor_optix.strategy.comparator ): MIN_EVALUATIONS = 3 def compare_candidate(store: ExperimentStore, candidate_id: str, task_env: str, *, margin: float = 0.0) -> StrategyComparison: """Gates on lo95(outcome_delta) > margin AND n_evaluations >= 3 -- the pessimistic CI bound, not the mean; hard floor on distinct seeds.""" def compare_against_approved(store: ExperimentStore, candidate_id: str, task_env: str, *, margin: float = 0.0) -> StrategyComparison: """As above, plus recomputes (never cached) each currently-approved strategy's own interval for the same task_env for a head-to-head check.""" Promotion ( tensor_optix.strategy.promotion ): class PromotionPolicy: def __init__( self, store: ExperimentStore, *, margin: float = 0.0, min_seeds: int = 3, min_held_out_tasks: int = 1, max_compute_ratio: float = 1.5, approval_mode: str = "human", # "human" | "auto" -- ValueError otherwise ): ... def evaluate(self, candidate_id: str, *, train_task_envs: List[str], held_out_task_envs: List[str]) -> PromotionVerdict: """Six criteria: beats_baseline_margin, repeats_across_seeds, generalizes_held_out, meets_compute_constraints, reproducible, human_reviewed. In approval_mode="human" (default), human_reviewed can only become True via a prior, separate store.approve_strategy() call -- evaluate() never calls it. In approval_mode="auto", if the other five all pass, evaluate() calls approve_strategy() itself with reviewer="auto:PromotionPolicy" -- always traceable, never silent.""" @dataclass class PromotionVerdict: candidate_id: str approved: bool criteria: Dict[str, bool] rationale: str @dataclass class StrategyScope: task_envs: List[str] held_out_task_envs: List[str] algorithms: List[str] # exact strings tested, never "all" frameworks: List[str] budget_range_episodes: Tuple[int, int] n_seeds_per_task: int excluded_agents: List[str] confound_notes: str def record_candidate_scope(store, candidate, *, train_task_envs, held_out_task_envs, algorithms, frameworks, budget_range_episodes, n_seeds_per_task, excluded_agents=None, confound_notes="") -> StrategyScope: ...

Never calls approve_strategy.""" def issue_recommendation(store, candidate, verdict, *, experiment_id) -> None: """Appends one EventRecord(event_type="recommendation_issued") -- an auditable record, not a vanishing print line.""" @dataclass class RuntimeConfig: task_env: str = "CartPole-v1" algorithm: str = "PPO" study_id: str = "live_runtime_cartpole_v1" solve_threshold: float = 475.0 eval_episodes: int = 5 cycle_sleep_s: float = 1.0 research_cycle_every: int = 3 experiment_budget_trials: int = 2 experiment_trial_steps: int = 3_000 experiment_seeds: Tuple[int, ...] = (0, 1, 2) max_cycles: int = 6 source_task_envs: Tuple[str, ...] = () # Deliberately NO approval_mode field -- no parameter path reaches # PromotionPolicy's approval_mode from here. class LiveAdaptiveRuntime: def __init__(self, store: ExperimentStore, config: RuntimeConfig, *, agent_factory, pipeline_factory): ... def run(self) -> Tuple[List[ObservationResult], List[CycleRecommendation]]: """Single-threaded sequential loop, bounded by max_cycles. docs.text: Method evidence. StrategySelector and NanonetsSelector count a ledger experiment as evidence for a method when config["sampler"] == method (trial-search runs) or config["op_name"] == method with is_baseline false (strategy-candidate runs). The live runtime's proposals over strategy ops therefore learn from earlier strategy trials. Untried methods are ranked last. CycleRecommendation.automatable_criteria_passed is True when every evidence-based criterion passed, ignoring human_reviewed (which the recommend-only loop never sets). Trial workers ( ConcurrentTrialScheduler , StrategyTrialRunner ) seed torch , numpy and random from the trial seed. CheckpointRollbackOp in a strategy trial rolls back to the run's current best checkpoint (it shares the run's CheckpointRegistry ). OptimizationMethodChoiceOp switches at most once per stall; after the run improves again, the next stall advances to the next entry of candidate_methods . run_reevaluation evaluates epsilon-greedy agents greedily ( epsilon = 0 ).
