docs.text: tensor_optix.ml_core An ML-native training core: fit() / predict() / evaluate() instead of act() / learn() , epochs and batches instead of episodes, real classification/regression metrics instead of mean episode return. Reuses CheckpointRegistry , BackoffScheduler , and SPSAOptimizer from the RL core unmodified. All three are algorithm-agnostic already. Does not replace or remove tensor_optix.ml 's MLAgent / DatasetPipeline path, which still works unchanged. BaseMLModel class BaseMLModel(ABC): """ The only contract between a trained ML model and tensor-optix's ML-native checkpointing/metrics machinery. """ def predict(self, X: Any) -> Any: """Run inference on a batch of inputs. Must not update weights.""" def train_step(self, batch: Any) -> float: """One gradient step on a single batch. Returns the scalar loss (a Python float, not a framework tensor).""" def evaluate(self, data) -> MLMetrics: """Run inference over an entire dataset/loader and compute MLMetrics via resolve_metrics().""" def iter_batches(self, data, batch_size: int, augment=None): """Yield framework-appropriate batches from a raw (X, y) pair or a native Dataset/DataLoader/tf.data.Dataset -- auto-detected. augment, if given, is applied per-batch and only takes effect for the raw (X, y) array form.""" def save_weights(self, path: str) -> None: ... def load_weights(self, path: str) -> None: ... def get_hyperparams(self) -> HyperparamSet: """Default: no tunable hyperparameters. Override to enable SPSA.""" def set_hyperparams(self, hyperparams: HyperparamSet) -> None: """Default: no-op.""" default_param_bounds: Dict[str, tuple] = {} default_log_params: List[str] = [] def average_weights(self, paths: List[str]) -> None: """Stochastic Weight Averaging across checkpoints. Default: no-op.""" def fit( self, train_data, val_data=None, epochs: int = 10, batch_size: int = 32, early_stopping_patience: Optional[int] = None, metrics="auto", callbacks: Optional[List] = None, checkpoint_dir: Optional[str] = None, lr_schedule: Optional[Callable[[int], float]] = None, augment: Optional[Callable] = None, ) -> FitHistory: """ Train for up to `epochs` epochs. If val_data is given and early_stopping_patience is set, stops early once the validation primary_score hasn't improved for that many consecutive epochs, and restores the best checkpoint's weights before returning. "New best" is tracked independently of whether checkpoint_dir is set -- early stopping works even with no disk checkpointing. lr_schedule: callable(epoch) -> float, applied once per epoch. Mutually exclusive with SPSA tuning of learning_rate for this run (see tensor_optix.ml_core.lr_schedules). augment: callable(X_batch, y_batch) -> (X_batch, y_batch), applied to every training batch (never validation). Only takes effect on the raw (X, y) array input form. """ FitHistory @dataclass class FitHistory: """Per-epoch record of training, returned by fit().""" train_loss: List[float] # mean training loss per epoch val_metrics: List[MLMetrics] # one MLMetrics per epoch (only if val_data given) best_epoch: Optional[int] # index of the best-scoring epoch stopped_early: bool # True if early stopping fired epochs_run: int # actual epochs completed (<= epochs if stopped early) Trainer class Trainer: """ Drives BaseMLModel.fit()'s actual epoch loop. Not part of the public BaseMLModel API -- constructed and run internally by fit(). Per epoch: 1. Iterate train_data in batches, call model.train_step() on each. A raw (X, y) pair is re-shuffled with a fresh random permutation every epoch (numpy global RNG); native Dataset / DataLoader / tf.data.Dataset inputs are passed through untouched. 2. If val_data given, call model.evaluate(val_data) -> MLMetrics. 3. Compare MLMetrics.primary_score against the best score seen this run. On improvement: reset the early-stopping counter, record the epoch as best, and (if checkpoint_dir is set) call CheckpointRegistry.save(). On no improvement: advance the early-stopping counter and feed BackoffScheduler.record_non_improvement(). 4. If an SPSA-tunable model (default_param_bounds set), call SPSAOptimizer.suggest() with the accumulated EvalMetrics history and apply the suggestion via model.set_hyperparams(). 5. Stop if early_stopping_patience epochs have passed with no improvement. After the loop, if checkpoint_dir was set and at least one checkpoint was saved, restores the best checkpoint's weights via CheckpointRegistry.load_best() before returning. """ def __init__( self, model, epochs: int, batch_size: int, early_stopping_patience: Optional[int], metrics, callbacks: Optional[List], checkpoint_dir: Optional[str], lr_schedule: Optional[Callable[[int], float]] = None, augment: Optional[Callable] = None, ): ... def run(self, train_data, val_data) -> FitHistory: ... # BackoffScheduler defaults used by Trainer -- re-tuned from the RL core's # defaults (trend_window=8, score_window=20, noise_k=2.0) for per-epoch # validation curves, which are typically smoother and evaluated far less # often than per-episode RL reward. ML_BACKOFF_DEFAULTS = dict( trend_window=4, score_window=8, noise_k=1.0, plateau_threshold=5, dormant_threshold=20, min_episodes_before_degradation=3, ) MLMetrics @dataclass class MLMetrics: """Scored output from a BaseMLModel's evaluate() call.""" primary_score: float # higher-is-better; feeds CheckpointRegistry/BackoffScheduler loss: float # raw loss value, for display only task_type: str # "classification" | "regression" | "other" metrics: Dict[str, float] # accuracy, f1_macro, confusion_matrix_<i>_<j>, mae, r2, ... epoch: int def to_eval_metrics(self) -> EvalMetrics: """Bridge to the RL core's EvalMetrics, so CheckpointRegistry (which only knows EvalMetrics) needs zero changes.""" Metrics registry def resolve_metrics( metrics: Union[str, List[Callable]], y_true: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, y_pred: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, n_classes: Optional[int] = None, loss: float = 0.0, epoch: int = 0, ) -> MLMetrics: """ Compute an MLMetrics from (y_true, y_pred), auto-detecting task type from y_true's dtype/values when metrics="auto" (default): integer or whole-number-valued-with-few-unique-values targets -> classification, continuous float targets -> regression. Mirrors tensor_optix.ml.loss_registry.resolve_loss()'s "auto" pattern. """ def available_metrics() -> str: """Human-readable list of all supported metric task types.""" metrics= Computed keys ( MLMetrics.metrics ) primary_score "classification" accuracy , precision_macro , recall_macro , f1_macro , per-class precision_<i> / recall_<i> / f1_<i> , flattened confusion_matrix_<i>_<j> accuracy "regression" mae , rmse , r2 r2 a list of (y_true, y_pred) -> float callables one key per callable, named by __name__ -loss metrics_impl/classification.py and metrics_impl/regression.py implement the underlying metric math in pure numpy. Both adapters convert their tensors to numpy before calling these, so the implementation is framework-agnostic: def confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, n_classes) -> np.ndarray: ... def accuracy(y_true, y_pred) -> float: ... def precision_recall_f1(cm) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]: ... def classification_metrics(y_true, y_pred, n_classes) -> Dict[str, float]: ... def unflatten_confusion_matrix(metrics, n_classes) -> np.ndarray: """Inverse of classification_metrics()'s confusion_matrix_<i>_<j> flattening, for display/plotting.""" def mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred) -> float: ... def root_mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred) -> float: ... def r2_score(y_true, y_pred) -> float: ... def regression_metrics(y_true, y_pred) -> Dict[str, float]: ... Adapters class TorchMLModel(BaseMLModel): """ Parameters ---------- model: Any nn.Module. loss_fn: Instantiated loss nn.Module, or any callable (pred, target) -> scalar. learning_rate, weight_decay: Adam hyperparameters. Tunable online via SPSA. max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping norm. None disables. device: "auto", "cpu", or "cuda". metrics: Passed through to evaluate() as resolve_metrics()'s metrics arg. default_param_bounds = {"learning_rate": (1e-5, 1e-2), "weight_decay": (0.0, 1e-2)} """ class TFMLModel(BaseMLModel): """ Parameters ---------- model: Any tf.keras.Model. loss_fn: A tf.keras.losses.Loss instance, or any callable (y_true, y_pred) -> scalar. learning_rate, weight_decay: AdamW when weight_decay > 0, plain Adam otherwise (TF's base Adam has no weight_decay kwarg). max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping norm. None disables. metrics: Passed through to evaluate() as resolve_metrics()'s metrics arg. default_param_bounds = {"learning_rate": (1e-5, 1e-2), "weight_decay": (0.0, 1e-2)} """ class FlaxMLModel(BaseMLModel): """ JAX/Flax NNX adapter. Conventions mirror tensor_optix.algorithms.flax_ppo, the only other Flax NNX code in the codebase: nnx.Optimizer for the update step, nnx.value_and_grad for the gradient, nnx.state/to_pure_dict + replace_by_pure_dict/update for weight save/load. Parameters ---------- model: Any flax.nnx.Module. Called as model(x). loss_fn: callable(pred, target) -> scalar jax array. There is no Flax equivalent of an instantiated loss object, so this is always a plain function (e.g. wrapping optax.softmax_cross_entropy_ with_integer_labels to reduce to a scalar). learning_rate, weight_decay: optax.adamw when weight_decay > 0, plain optax.adam otherwise. max_grad_norm: applied via optax.clip_by_global_norm in the optax.chain. None disables. metrics: Passed through to evaluate() as resolve_metrics()'s metrics arg. default_param_bounds = {"learning_rate": (1e-5, 1e-2), "weight_decay": (0.0, 1e-2)} """ Shuffling: the adapters' iter_batches() walk a raw (X, y) pair in storage order - Trainer permutes the pair once per epoch before handing it over, so training batches differ between epochs while evaluate() stays deterministic. Seed with np.random.seed(...) for reproducible runs. A DataLoader / tf.data.Dataset keeps whatever shuffle configuration you built it with. All three adapters' iter_batches() accept a raw (X, y) array pair, or a native Dataset / DataLoader (Torch) / tf.data.Dataset (TF), auto-detected by type. FlaxMLModel accepts only the raw (X, y) form -- there is no Dataset/DataLoader equivalent in this codebase's JAX dependency set. lr_schedules class StepLR: """base_lr * gamma**(epoch // step_size).""" def __init__(self, base_lr: float, step_size: int, gamma: float = 0.1): ... def __call__(self, epoch: int) -> float: ... class CosineAnnealingLR: """Cosine decay from base_lr to min_lr over `epochs` total epochs.""" def __init__(self, base_lr: float, epochs: int, min_lr: float = 0.0): ... def __call__(self, epoch: int) -> float: ... class WarmupLR: """Linear warmup from 0 to base_lr over warmup_epochs, then delegates to `after` (any other schedule) for epochs >= warmup_epochs, re-based to 0 at that point.""" def __init__(self, base_lr: float, warmup_epochs: int, after: Optional[object] = None): ... def __call__(self, epoch: int) -> float: ... Any callable(epoch: int) -> float works as lr_schedule -- these three are provided for convenience, not a closed interface. transfer def freeze_layers(model, layers: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> None: """Freeze parameters/layers in-place. model: nn.Module or tf.keras.Model. layers: submodule names (Torch, model.named_modules()) or layer names (TF, layer.name) to target. None freezes the whole model.""" def unfreeze_layers(model, layers: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> None: """Inverse of freeze_layers().""" def load_pretrained_backbone( name: str, framework: str = "torch", pretrained: bool = True, freeze: bool = False, input_shape: Optional[tuple] = None, ): """ Load a common pretrained backbone with its classifier head removed. Torch: name is a torchvision.models function name (resnet18, resnet34, resnet50, resnet101, resnet152, vgg11/13/16/19, densenet121/169/201, mobilenet_v2, mobilenet_v3_small/large, efficientnet_b0/b1/b2) -- head replaced with nn.Identity(). TF: name is a tf.keras.applications class name (e.g. ResNet50, MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0) -- loaded with include_top=False, which requires input_shape. Any other architecture: build it directly via torchvision.models/tf.keras.applications and strip the head yourself. """ See Train an ML model for the full guide. Classification metrics and single-output heads resolve_metrics(..., "classification") works on flat arrays of class indices. Two shapes are normalised before the confusion matrix is built: targets of shape (N, 1) are flattened; a single-output binary head, whose per-sample output is a raw logit or probability rather than a class index, is thresholded - at 0.5 when every value lies in [0, 1] (probabilities), at 0 otherwise (logits). Multi-class heads are already reduced with argmax by the adapters' evaluate() .

Returns the scalar loss (a Python float, not a framework tensor).""" def evaluate(self, data) -> MLMetrics: """Run inference over an entire dataset/loader and compute MLMetrics via resolve_metrics().""" def iter_batches(self, data, batch_size: int, augment=None): """Yield framework-appropriate batches from a raw (X, y) pair or a native Dataset/DataLoader/tf.data.Dataset -- auto-detected. augment, if given, is applied per-batch and only takes effect for the raw (X, y) array form.""" def save_weights(self, path: str) -> None: ... def load_weights(self, path: str) -> None: ... def get_hyperparams(self) -> HyperparamSet: """Default: no tunable hyperparameters. Override to enable SPSA.""" def set_hyperparams(self, hyperparams: HyperparamSet) -> None: """Default: no-op.""" default_param_bounds: Dict[str, tuple] = {} default_log_params: List[str] = [] def average_weights(self, paths: List[str]) -> None: """Stochastic Weight Averaging across checkpoints. Default: no-op.""" def fit( self, train_data, val_data=None, epochs: int = 10, batch_size: int = 32, early_stopping_patience: Optional[int] = None, metrics="auto", callbacks: Optional[List] = None, checkpoint_dir: Optional[str] = None, lr_schedule: Optional[Callable[[int], float]] = None, augment: Optional[Callable] = None, ) -> FitHistory: """ Train for up to `epochs` epochs. If val_data is given and early_stopping_patience is set, stops early once the validation primary_score hasn't improved for that many consecutive epochs, and restores the best checkpoint's weights before returning. "New best" is tracked independently of whether checkpoint_dir is set -- early stopping works even with no disk checkpointing. lr_schedule: callable(epoch) -> float, applied once per epoch. Mutually exclusive with SPSA tuning of learning_rate for this run (see tensor_optix.ml_core.lr_schedules). augment: callable(X_batch, y_batch) -> (X_batch, y_batch), applied to every training batch (never validation). Only takes effect on the raw (X, y) array input form. """

docs.text: class Trainer: """ Drives BaseMLModel.fit()'s actual epoch loop. Not part of the public BaseMLModel API -- constructed and run internally by fit(). Per epoch: 1. Iterate train_data in batches, call model.train_step() on each. A raw (X, y) pair is re-shuffled with a fresh random permutation every epoch (numpy global RNG); native Dataset / DataLoader / tf.data.Dataset inputs are passed through untouched. 2. If val_data given, call model.evaluate(val_data) -> MLMetrics. 3. Compare MLMetrics.primary_score against the best score seen this run. On improvement: reset the early-stopping counter, record the epoch as best, and (if checkpoint_dir is set) call CheckpointRegistry.save(). On no improvement: advance the early-stopping counter and feed BackoffScheduler.record_non_improvement(). 4. If an SPSA-tunable model (default_param_bounds set), call SPSAOptimizer.suggest() with the accumulated EvalMetrics history and apply the suggestion via model.set_hyperparams(). 5. Stop if early_stopping_patience epochs have passed with no improvement. After the loop, if checkpoint_dir was set and at least one checkpoint was saved, restores the best checkpoint's weights via CheckpointRegistry.load_best() before returning. """ def __init__( self, model, epochs: int, batch_size: int, early_stopping_patience: Optional[int], metrics, callbacks: Optional[List], checkpoint_dir: Optional[str], lr_schedule: Optional[Callable[[int], float]] = None, augment: Optional[Callable] = None, ): ... def run(self, train_data, val_data) -> FitHistory: ... # BackoffScheduler defaults used by Trainer -- re-tuned from the RL core's # defaults (trend_window=8, score_window=20, noise_k=2.0) for per-epoch # validation curves, which are typically smoother and evaluated far less # often than per-episode RL reward. ML_BACKOFF_DEFAULTS = dict( trend_window=4, score_window=8, noise_k=1.0, plateau_threshold=5, dormant_threshold=20, min_episodes_before_degradation=3, )

docs.text: def resolve_metrics( metrics: Union[str, List[Callable]], y_true: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, y_pred: Optional[np.ndarray] = None, n_classes: Optional[int] = None, loss: float = 0.0, epoch: int = 0, ) -> MLMetrics: """ Compute an MLMetrics from (y_true, y_pred), auto-detecting task type from y_true's dtype/values when metrics="auto" (default): integer or whole-number-valued-with-few-unique-values targets -> classification, continuous float targets -> regression. Mirrors tensor_optix.ml.loss_registry.resolve_loss()'s "auto" pattern. """ def available_metrics() -> str: """Human-readable list of all supported metric task types.""" metrics= Computed keys ( MLMetrics.metrics ) primary_score "classification" accuracy , precision_macro , recall_macro , f1_macro , per-class precision_<i> / recall_<i> / f1_<i> , flattened confusion_matrix_<i>_<j> accuracy "regression" mae , rmse , r2 r2 a list of (y_true, y_pred) -> float callables one key per callable, named by __name__ -loss metrics_impl/classification.py and metrics_impl/regression.py implement the underlying metric math in pure numpy. Both adapters convert their tensors to numpy before calling these, so the implementation is framework-agnostic: def confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred, n_classes) -> np.ndarray: ... def accuracy(y_true, y_pred) -> float: ... def precision_recall_f1(cm) -> Dict[str, np.ndarray]: ... def classification_metrics(y_true, y_pred, n_classes) -> Dict[str, float]: ... def unflatten_confusion_matrix(metrics, n_classes) -> np.ndarray: """Inverse of classification_metrics()'s confusion_matrix_<i>_<j> flattening, for display/plotting.""" def mean_absolute_error(y_true, y_pred) -> float: ... def root_mean_squared_error(y_true, y_pred) -> float: ... def r2_score(y_true, y_pred) -> float: ... def regression_metrics(y_true, y_pred) -> Dict[str, float]: ...

docs.text: class TorchMLModel(BaseMLModel): """ Parameters ---------- model: Any nn.Module. loss_fn: Instantiated loss nn.Module, or any callable (pred, target) -> scalar. learning_rate, weight_decay: Adam hyperparameters. Tunable online via SPSA. max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping norm. None disables. device: "auto", "cpu", or "cuda". metrics: Passed through to evaluate() as resolve_metrics()'s metrics arg. default_param_bounds = {"learning_rate": (1e-5, 1e-2), "weight_decay": (0.0, 1e-2)} """ class TFMLModel(BaseMLModel): """ Parameters ---------- model: Any tf.keras.Model. loss_fn: A tf.keras.losses.Loss instance, or any callable (y_true, y_pred) -> scalar. learning_rate, weight_decay: AdamW when weight_decay > 0, plain Adam otherwise (TF's base Adam has no weight_decay kwarg). max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping norm. None disables. metrics: Passed through to evaluate() as resolve_metrics()'s metrics arg. default_param_bounds = {"learning_rate": (1e-5, 1e-2), "weight_decay": (0.0, 1e-2)} """ class FlaxMLModel(BaseMLModel): """ JAX/Flax NNX adapter. Conventions mirror tensor_optix.algorithms.flax_ppo, the only other Flax NNX code in the codebase: nnx.Optimizer for the update step, nnx.value_and_grad for the gradient, nnx.state/to_pure_dict + replace_by_pure_dict/update for weight save/load. Parameters ---------- model: Any flax.nnx.Module. Called as model(x). loss_fn: callable(pred, target) -> scalar jax array. There is no Flax equivalent of an instantiated loss object, so this is always a plain function (e.g. wrapping optax.softmax_cross_entropy_ with_integer_labels to reduce to a scalar). learning_rate, weight_decay: optax.adamw when weight_decay > 0, plain optax.adam otherwise. max_grad_norm: applied via optax.clip_by_global_norm in the optax.chain. None disables. metrics: Passed through to evaluate() as resolve_metrics()'s metrics arg. default_param_bounds = {"learning_rate": (1e-5, 1e-2), "weight_decay": (0.0, 1e-2)} """ Shuffling: the adapters' iter_batches() walk a raw (X, y) pair in storage order - Trainer permutes the pair once per epoch before handing it over, so training batches differ between epochs while evaluate() stays deterministic. Seed with np.random.seed(...) for reproducible runs. A DataLoader / tf.data.Dataset keeps whatever shuffle configuration you built it with. All three adapters' iter_batches() accept a raw (X, y) array pair, or a native Dataset / DataLoader (Torch) / tf.data.Dataset (TF), auto-detected by type. FlaxMLModel accepts only the raw (X, y) form -- there is no Dataset/DataLoader equivalent in this codebase's JAX dependency set.

Any callable(epoch: int) -> float works as lr_schedule -- these three are provided for convenience, not a closed interface.

None freezes the whole model.""" def unfreeze_layers(model, layers: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> None: """Inverse of freeze_layers().""" def load_pretrained_backbone( name: str, framework: str = "torch", pretrained: bool = True, freeze: bool = False, input_shape: Optional[tuple] = None, ): """ Load a common pretrained backbone with its classifier head removed. Torch: name is a torchvision.models function name (resnet18, resnet34, resnet50, resnet101, resnet152, vgg11/13/16/19, densenet121/169/201, mobilenet_v2, mobilenet_v3_small/large, efficientnet_b0/b1/b2) -- head replaced with nn.Identity(). TF: name is a tf.keras.applications class name (e.g. ResNet50, MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0) -- loaded with include_top=False, which requires input_shape. Any other architecture: build it directly via torchvision.models/tf.keras.applications and strip the head yourself. """ See Train an ML model for the full guide.

docs.text: resolve_metrics(..., "classification") works on flat arrays of class indices. Two shapes are normalised before the confusion matrix is built: targets of shape (N, 1) are flattened; a single-output binary head, whose per-sample output is a raw logit or probability rather than a class index, is thresholded - at 0.5 when every value lies in [0, 1] (probabilities), at 0 otherwise (logits). Multi-class heads are already reduced with argmax by the adapters' evaluate() .

docs.text: tensor_optix.ml Adapts the training loop to general (non-RL) ML tasks: supervised, autoencoder, VAE, and contrastive learning. MLAgent class MLAgent(BaseAgent): """ BaseAgent adapter for any nn.Module training task. Wraps any nn.Module and gives it the full tensor-optix feature set: - SPSA online hyperparameter tuning - Rollback on validation degradation - Convergence / plateau detection - Checkpointing (save / load weights) - Weight averaging (SWA) Works for: supervised classification/regression, unsupervised autoencoders/VAE, self-supervised contrastive learning (SimCLR), or anything with a loss. Parameters ---------- model: Any nn.Module. loss_fn: Instantiated loss nn.Module (build via loss_registry.resolve_loss()). learning_rate: Initial Adam learning rate. Tunable online via SPSA. weight_decay: Adam L2 regularisation. Tunable online via SPSA. max_grad_norm: Gradient clipping norm. None disables. device: "auto", "cpu", or "cuda". """ is_on_policy = True # safe for rollback - each batch is independent data default_param_bounds = {"learning_rate": (1e-5, 1e-2), "weight_decay": (0.0, 1e-2)} default_log_params = ["learning_rate"] def act(self, observation): """Inference - returns raw model output as a numpy array.""" def learn(self, episode_data: EpisodeData) -> dict: """ One gradient update on the batch packed into episode_data. Mapping from EpisodeData fields: observations → model input (X) actions → target (y, or X again for reconstruction/VAE) For unsupervised tasks the pipeline sets actions = observations so the loss receives the original input as the target automatically. """ DatasetPipeline class DatasetPipeline(BasePipeline): """ Adapts a PyTorch Dataset or DataLoader to BasePipeline. Each "episode" is one mini-batch. Loops through the dataset indefinitely - the loop controller decides when to stop, never the pipeline. Mapping to EpisodeData: observations → input tensor X actions → target tensor y, OR X again for unsupervised tasks rewards → [-loss] placeholder filled by MLAgent.learn() terminated → [True] - one "episode" per batch. truncated → [False] Parameters ---------- dataset: Dataset or DataLoader. A Dataset is wrapped in a DataLoader automatically using batch_size and shuffle. batch_size: Batch size when building a DataLoader from a Dataset. shuffle: Whether to shuffle each epoch. Default True. loss_key: When an unsupervised key ("reconstruction", "vae", "contrastive"), sets actions = observations automatically. num_workers, pin_memory: DataLoader passthrough. """ Loss registry def resolve_loss(loss, dataset=None, n_samples: int = 64) -> nn.Module: """ Return an instantiated loss nn.Module. loss: "auto", a loss key string, or an nn.Module instance. dataset: required when loss="auto" - used to sample items for detection. """ def available_losses() -> str: """Human-readable list of all supported loss strings.""" Auto-detection rules ( loss="auto" ), in order: Items are single tensors (no label) → "reconstruction" Items are pairs (x1, x2) of same shape → "contrastive" Targets are int/long → "cross_entropy" Targets are float, values in {0, 1} → "bce" Targets are float, any range → "mse" String Criterion Use case "cross_entropy" nn.CrossEntropyLoss multi-class classification "bce" nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss binary classification "mse" nn.MSELoss regression "mae" nn.L1Loss regression, outlier-robust "huber" nn.HuberLoss regression, very outlier-robust "cosine" nn.CosineEmbeddingLoss embedding / similarity "reconstruction" MSE(output, input) autoencoders "vae" ELBO (reconstruction + KL) VAEs - model must return (reconstruction, mu, logvar) "contrastive" NT-Xent SimCLR - dataset yields (x1, x2) pairs Any nn.Module or callable can be passed directly as loss= instead of a string. See Train any PyTorch model (ML mode) for the simplified Optimizer(model, dataset, ...) entry point.

docs.text: tensor_optix.multi_agent Pipelines and a minimal runner for PettingZoo multi-agent environments. Each seat (PettingZoo agent id) is driven by its own ordinary BaseAgent ; a window yields one EpisodeData per seat. pip install tensor-optix[torch,pettingzoo] from tensor_optix.multi_agent import ( SeatEnvView, ParallelMultiAgentPipeline, AECMultiAgentPipeline, MultiAgentRunner, SelfPlayConfig, SelfPlayPipeline, OpponentPool, ) MultiAgentEpisodeData (in tensor_optix.multi_agent.multi_agent_episode ) is the alias Dict[Hashable, EpisodeData] - the type both pipelines yield. SeatEnvView class SeatEnvView: """ A single seat's view of a PettingZoo env: exposes .observation_space and .action_space for one agent id, so make_agent(view) can build that seat's agent exactly as it would for a Gymnasium env. Discrete observation spaces are presented as a one-hot Box(n,) - make_agent() needs a Box observation space. """ def __init__(self, pz_env, agent_id): ... def encode_observation(self, raw_observation): """One-hot encode a Discrete observation; pass anything else through.""" Pass the views to a pipeline's views= argument so observations are encoded the same way the agent's network was sized. ParallelMultiAgentPipeline class ParallelMultiAgentPipeline: """ Drives a PettingZoo ParallelEnv: every active seat acts each round. window_size: rounds collected per yielded window (each active seat contributes one step per round). views: optional {agent_id: SeatEnvView} for observation encoding. """ def __init__(self, env, agents: Dict[Hashable, Any], window_size: int = 200, views=None): ... def set_agents(self, agents) -> None: ... def setup(self) -> None: ... def episodes(self) -> Generator[Dict[Hashable, EpisodeData], None, None]: ... def teardown(self) -> None: ... When every seat is done the env is reset and the window keeps filling, mirroring BatchPipeline . AECMultiAgentPipeline class AECMultiAgentPipeline: """ Drives a PettingZoo AECEnv (turn-based, one seat acts per env.step()). window_size: TOTAL env.step() calls per window, split across whichever seats take turns during it - not window_size per seat. """ def __init__(self, env, agents: Dict[Hashable, Any], window_size: int = 200, views=None): ... Reward alignment. In the AEC API, env.last() returns the reward a seat accumulated since its previous action . The pipeline credits that reward - and the terminated / truncated flag observed on the seat's final action=None turn - back to the seat's previously recorded step. So within a seat's EpisodeData : rewards[k] is the outcome of actions[k] . A seat's last acted step of an episode carries the terminal reward with terminated (or truncated ) set, so dones marks real episode boundaries for GAE / n-step returns. No un-acted-on step is ever appended, so agents' act() -populated rollout caches stay in sync with rewards . Known limitation. The outcome of a seat's last action in a window only arrives on its next turn, which belongs to the next window. That one reward per seat per window boundary is not credited (the step keeps reward 0.0 and no done flag). final_obs is None for AEC windows - there is no per-seat post-window observation to bootstrap from. A seat that gets no turn in a window yields an empty EpisodeData ; skip learn() for it ( MultiAgentRunner does). MultiAgentRunner class MultiAgentRunner: """ Trains every seat and applies, per seat, the convergence and checkpoint machinery of the single-agent loop. """ def __init__( self, pipeline, agents: Dict[Hashable, Any], *, evaluator=None, # BaseEvaluator, or {agent_id: BaseEvaluator} checkpoint_dir: Optional[str] = None, max_snapshots: int = 10, improvement_margin: float = 0.0, plateau_threshold: int = 5, dormant_threshold: int = 20, min_windows_before_dormant: int = 0, min_completed_episodes_before_converged: int = 10, noise_k: float = 2.0, score_window: int = 20, trend_window: int = 8, optimizer="auto", # per-seat tuning: "auto" | None | callable(agent) | {agent_id: optimizer} self_play: Optional[SelfPlayConfig] = None, rollback_on_degradation: bool = False, degradation_threshold: float = 0.95, min_consecutive_degradations: int = 3, stop_when: str = "all", # "all" | "any" stop_on_convergence: bool = True, restore_best: bool = True, callbacks: Optional[List[Any]] = None, ): ... def run(self, max_windows: Optional[int] = None) -> MultiAgentRunResult: ... def stop(self) -> None: ... def add_callback(self, callback) -> None: ... @property def states(self) -> Dict[Hashable, LoopState]: ... @property def best_scores(self) -> Dict[Hashable, Optional[float]]: ... @property def best_snapshots(self) -> Dict[Hashable, Optional[PolicySnapshot]]: ... Each window, for every seat that took at least one step: agent.learn(episode_data) . The window is scored by evaluator (default: mean return of the episodes that completed in the window - the same default the single-agent loop uses). Checkpoint. If the score beats the seat's best by more than improvement_margin , the seat is saved to its own CheckpointRegistry under <checkpoint_dir>/<agent_id> . With checkpoint_dir=None best scores are still tracked but nothing is written or restored. Convergence. The score feeds the seat's own BackoffScheduler . A seat whose score trend stays flat for plateau_threshold consecutive windows is COOLING ; after dormant_threshold it is DORMANT , i.e. converged. A later upward trend puts it back to ACTIVE . Every window is evaluated (no eval-interval backoff). A seat with no turn in a window is skipped entirely - not learned, not scored, and not counted toward its plateau counter. Scores are finished-episode returns. The pipelines track each seat's return across windows. A window in which a seat finished no episode still trains that seat but is not scored (no checkpoint, no plateau count). Until a seat's first episode finishes its windows are scored by mean per-step reward; when it does, that seat's best score and trend are reset because the scale changes. A seat cannot plateau or converge before min_completed_episodes_before_converged (default 10 ) episodes have finished - set it to 0 for environments whose episodes never end. SeatResult.completed_episodes reports the count. When the run stops Condition stop_reason every seat converged ( stop_when="all" , default) or the first seat converged ( stop_when="any" ) "converged" max_windows reached "max_windows" stop() called (e.g. from a callback) "stopped" the pipeline's generator ended "pipeline_exhausted" stop_on_convergence=False disables the first row. The default is "all" because in a competitive game one seat plateauing while its opponent still improves is not convergence. Best-weight restore. When the run ends (including on an exception) and restore_best=True , every seat with a checkpoint is restored to its best snapshot. In competitive games each seat's best score was achieved against the opponents as they were at that time , so restored seats can come from different stages of training; pass restore_best=False to keep the final, jointly trained weights - the best snapshots remain on disk and in the result. @dataclass class MultiAgentRunResult: windows_run: int stop_reason: str seats: Dict[Hashable, SeatResult] converged: bool # property: stop_reason == "converged" @dataclass class SeatResult: agent_id: Hashable state: LoopState converged: bool windows_scored: int completed_episodes: int best_score: Optional[float] last_score: Optional[float] best_snapshot: Optional[PolicySnapshot] frozen_windows: int # windows played by a pool snapshot (self-play) degradations: int # confirmed degradations rollbacks: int # of which restored the best checkpoint hyperparams: Optional[dict] # the seat's hyperparameters at the end of the run MultiAgentRunResult.pool_sizes reports the number of self-play snapshots held per seat. MultiAgentCallback class MultiAgentCallback: def on_run_start(self) -> None: ... def on_window_end(self, window_id: int, metrics: Dict[Hashable, EvalMetrics]) -> None: ... def on_improvement(self, agent_id, snapshot: Optional[PolicySnapshot], score: float) -> None: ... def on_plateau(self, agent_id, window_id: int) -> None: ... def on_converged(self, agent_id, window_id: int) -> None: ... def on_hyperparam_update(self, agent_id, old_params: dict, new_params: dict) -> None: ... def on_degradation(self, agent_id, window_id: int, score: float, rolled_back: bool) -> None: ... def on_run_stop(self, reason: str) -> None: ... Subclassing is optional - any object defining some of these methods works. An exception raised by a callback is logged and does not stop training. Per-seat hyperparameter tuning Every seat has its own optimizer, driven by that seat's own scores - the same online tuning RLOptimizer performs for a single agent. optimizer= Result "auto" (default) an SPSAOptimizer over the agent's default_param_bounds / default_log_params , for each seat whose agent declares them; other seats are not tuned None no tuning callable(agent) -> BaseOptimizer called once per seat {agent_id: BaseOptimizer or None} explicit per seat A single optimizer instance cannot be shared between seats (optimizers hold per-run state); passing one with more than one seat raises ValueError . Windows that are not scored (no finished episode, no turn, or frozen for self-play) do not step the optimizer. A scored window is degraded when the seat's score is below best - max(|best| * (1 - degradation_threshold), noise floor) , where the noise floor is the seat's own adaptive floor (so ordinary score noise does not qualify). Training against a pool of past snapshots makes forgetting how to beat an old strategy cost reward. There are two ways to use it. @dataclass class SelfPlayConfig: pool_size: int = 10 # snapshots kept per seat, oldest evicted first snapshot_every: int = 20 # save a snapshot every N windows opponent_prob: float = 0.5 # MultiAgentRunner: chance per window that a seat is frozen pool_dir: Optional[str] = None # None = temporary directory, removed when the run ends opponent_factory: Optional[Callable[[Hashable], Any]] = None seed: Optional[int] = None # seeds the pool's sampling Snapshots are weights on disk. Each window, each seat whose pool is non-empty is frozen with probability opponent_prob : it is played by a uniformly sampled past snapshot of itself. At least one seat always stays live. """ def __init__(self, pipeline, learner_seat, agent=None, config: Optional[SelfPlayConfig] = None): ... def set_agent(self, agent) -> None: ... @property def pool(self) -> Optional[OpponentPool]: ... Because it is a BasePipeline , RLOptimizer / LoopController drive it with everything the single-agent loop has: every optimizer, rollback on degradation, policy spawning, checkpoint confirmation. The pool starts with the learner's initial weights and gains a snapshot every snapshot_every windows; each window every opponent seat is loaded with a uniformly sampled snapshot. The opponent seats must be playable by the learner's policy - same observation and action spaces (symmetric games). opponent_prob is not used here. Only the learner seat's EpisodeData is yielded; windows in which the learner took no step are skipped. With the AEC pipeline the learner gets roughly window_size / n_seats steps per window. """ def __init__(self, env, agents: Dict[Hashable, Any], window_size: int = 200, views=None): ... def set_agents(self, agents) -> None: ... def setup(self) -> None: ... def episodes(self) -> Generator[Dict[Hashable, EpisodeData], None, None]: ... def teardown(self) -> None: ... docs.text: class AECMultiAgentPipeline: """ Drives a PettingZoo AECEnv (turn-based, one seat acts per env.step()). window_size: TOTAL env.step() calls per window, split across whichever seats take turns during it - not window_size per seat. """ def __init__(self, env, agents: Dict[Hashable, Any], window_size: int = 200, views=None): ... Reward alignment. In the AEC API, env.last() returns the reward a seat accumulated since its previous action . The pipeline credits that reward - and the terminated / truncated flag observed on the seat's final action=None turn - back to the seat's previously recorded step. So within a seat's EpisodeData : rewards[k] is the outcome of actions[k] . A seat's last acted step of an episode carries the terminal reward with terminated (or truncated ) set, so dones marks real episode boundaries for GAE / n-step returns. No un-acted-on step is ever appended, so agents' act() -populated rollout caches stay in sync with rewards . Known limitation. The outcome of a seat's last action in a window only arrives on its next turn, which belongs to the next window. That one reward per seat per window boundary is not credited (the step keeps reward 0.0 and no done flag). final_obs is None for AEC windows - there is no per-seat post-window observation to bootstrap from. A seat that gets no turn in a window yields an empty EpisodeData ; skip learn() for it ( MultiAgentRunner does).

docs.text: class MultiAgentRunner: """ Trains every seat and applies, per seat, the convergence and checkpoint machinery of the single-agent loop. """ def __init__( self, pipeline, agents: Dict[Hashable, Any], *, evaluator=None, # BaseEvaluator, or {agent_id: BaseEvaluator} checkpoint_dir: Optional[str] = None, max_snapshots: int = 10, improvement_margin: float = 0.0, plateau_threshold: int = 5, dormant_threshold: int = 20, min_windows_before_dormant: int = 0, min_completed_episodes_before_converged: int = 10, noise_k: float = 2.0, score_window: int = 20, trend_window: int = 8, optimizer="auto", # per-seat tuning: "auto" | None | callable(agent) | {agent_id: optimizer} self_play: Optional[SelfPlayConfig] = None, rollback_on_degradation: bool = False, degradation_threshold: float = 0.95, min_consecutive_degradations: int = 3, stop_when: str = "all", # "all" | "any" stop_on_convergence: bool = True, restore_best: bool = True, callbacks: Optional[List[Any]] = None, ): ... def run(self, max_windows: Optional[int] = None) -> MultiAgentRunResult: ... def stop(self) -> None: ... def add_callback(self, callback) -> None: ... @property def states(self) -> Dict[Hashable, LoopState]: ... @property def best_scores(self) -> Dict[Hashable, Optional[float]]: ... @property def best_snapshots(self) -> Dict[Hashable, Optional[PolicySnapshot]]: ... Each window, for every seat that took at least one step: agent.learn(episode_data) . The window is scored by evaluator (default: mean return of the episodes that completed in the window - the same default the single-agent loop uses). Checkpoint. If the score beats the seat's best by more than improvement_margin , the seat is saved to its own CheckpointRegistry under <checkpoint_dir>/<agent_id> . With checkpoint_dir=None best scores are still tracked but nothing is written or restored. Convergence. The score feeds the seat's own BackoffScheduler . A seat whose score trend stays flat for plateau_threshold consecutive windows is COOLING ; after dormant_threshold it is DORMANT , i.e. converged. A later upward trend puts it back to ACTIVE . Every window is evaluated (no eval-interval backoff). A seat with no turn in a window is skipped entirely - not learned, not scored, and not counted toward its plateau counter. Scores are finished-episode returns. The pipelines track each seat's return across windows. A window in which a seat finished no episode still trains that seat but is not scored (no checkpoint, no plateau count). Until a seat's first episode finishes its windows are scored by mean per-step reward; when it does, that seat's best score and trend are reset because the scale changes. A seat cannot plateau or converge before min_completed_episodes_before_converged (default 10 ) episodes have finished - set it to 0 for environments whose episodes never end. SeatResult.completed_episodes reports the count. When the run stops Condition stop_reason every seat converged ( stop_when="all" , default) or the first seat converged ( stop_when="any" ) "converged" max_windows reached "max_windows" stop() called (e.g. from a callback) "stopped" the pipeline's generator ended "pipeline_exhausted" stop_on_convergence=False disables the first row. The default is "all" because in a competitive game one seat plateauing while its opponent still improves is not convergence. Best-weight restore. When the run ends (including on an exception) and restore_best=True , every seat with a checkpoint is restored to its best snapshot. In competitive games each seat's best score was achieved against the opponents as they were at that time , so restored seats can come from different stages of training; pass restore_best=False to keep the final, jointly trained weights - the best snapshots remain on disk and in the result. @dataclass class MultiAgentRunResult: windows_run: int stop_reason: str seats: Dict[Hashable, SeatResult] converged: bool # property: stop_reason == "converged" @dataclass class SeatResult: agent_id: Hashable state: LoopState converged: bool windows_scored: int completed_episodes: int best_score: Optional[float] last_score: Optional[float] best_snapshot: Optional[PolicySnapshot] frozen_windows: int # windows played by a pool snapshot (self-play) degradations: int # confirmed degradations rollbacks: int # of which restored the best checkpoint hyperparams: Optional[dict] # the seat's hyperparameters at the end of the run MultiAgentRunResult.pool_sizes reports the number of self-play snapshots held per seat.

docs.text: Top-level API: RLOptimizer and Optimizer RLOptimizer class RLOptimizer: """ Main public API. This is what users import. Assembles all components and delegates to LoopController. Sensible defaults for everything - minimal required args: agent, pipeline. Minimal usage: optimizer = RLOptimizer(agent=my_tf_agent, pipeline=my_pipeline) optimizer.run() With automatic trial-level hyperparameter search (TrialOrchestrator): optimizer = RLOptimizer( agent_factory=lambda params: MyAgent(params), pipeline_factory=lambda: MyPipeline(), param_space={ "learning_rate": ("log_float", 1e-4, 3e-3), "clip_ratio": ("float", 0.1, 0.3), }, n_trials=20, trial_steps_fraction=0.15, # 15% of max_steps per trial ) optimizer.run() # trial search runs first, then full training with best params When param_space + agent_factory + pipeline_factory are provided: 1. TrialOrchestrator runs n_trials independent short runs to find best params 2. agent_factory(best_params) creates the agent for the full run 3. The main RLOptimizer loop runs with those params + SPSA online adaptation The agent and pipeline args become optional when factories are provided. """ Constructor def __init__( self, agent: Optional[BaseAgent] = None, pipeline: Optional[BasePipeline] = None, evaluator: Optional[BaseEvaluator] = None, optimizer: Optional[BaseOptimizer] = None, checkpoint_dir: str = "./tensor_optix_checkpoints", max_snapshots: int = 10, rollback_on_degradation: bool = False, improvement_margin: float = 0.0, max_episodes: Optional[int] = None, base_interval: int = 1, backoff_factor: float = 2.0, max_interval_episodes: int = 100, plateau_threshold: int = 5, dormant_threshold: int = 20, degradation_threshold: float = 0.95, min_degradation_drop: float = 1e-4, noise_k: float = 2.0, score_window: int = 20, trend_window: int = 8, min_episodes_before_dormant: int = 0, min_episodes_before_degradation: int = 5, callbacks: Optional[List[LoopCallback]] = None, val_pipeline: Optional[BasePipeline] = None, score_smoothing: int = 2, checkpoint_score_fn=None, verbose: bool = False, verbose_log_file: Optional[str] = None, # ── DiagnosticController ── diag_loss_spike_factor: float = 5.0, diag_entropy_floor: Optional[float] = 0.05, diag_target_kl: Optional[float] = 0.02, diag_epsilon_patience: int = 20, diag_epsilon_reset_value: float = 0.3, diag_epsilon_score_threshold: float = 20.0, diag_min_episodes: int = 5, min_consecutive_degradations: int = 3, convergence_patience: int = 5, cv_threshold: float = 0.05, gap_threshold: float = 0.20, target_score: Optional[float] = None, # ── Trial-level search (TrialOrchestrator) ── agent_factory: Optional[Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], BaseAgent]] = None, pipeline_factory: Optional[Callable[[], BasePipeline]] = None, param_space: Optional[Dict[str, tuple]] = None, n_trials: int = 20, trial_steps_fraction: float = 0.01, val_pipeline_factory: Optional[Callable[[], BasePipeline]] = None, trial_agent_factory: Optional[Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], BaseAgent]] = None, ) Either agent or agent_factory must be provided, and either pipeline or pipeline_factory . RLOptimizer builds, internally: a TFEvaluator (default, if none given), an SPSAOptimizer seeded from the agent's default_param_bounds / default_log_params (if no optimizer given, or if a given SPSAOptimizer has no bounds yet), a CheckpointRegistry , a BackoffScheduler , and a DiagnosticController - then wraps them all in a LoopController . Off-policy agents ( agent.is_on_policy == False ) get more patient defaults automatically: if dormant_threshold is left at its default 20 , it's lowered to 15 ; if min_episodes_before_dormant is left at 0 , it's raised to agent.default_min_episodes_before_dormant (default 100 ). Methods def run(self) -> None: """ Start the autonomous loop. Blocks until stopped or max_episodes reached. If param_space + agent_factory + pipeline_factory were provided: 1. Runs TrialOrchestrator to find best hyperparameter configuration. 2. Calls agent_factory(best_params) and pipeline_factory() to build the agent and pipeline for the full training run. 3. Runs the main loop with those params + SPSA online adaptation. """ def add_callback(self, cb: LoopCallback) -> None: """ Register an additional callback. Safe to call before or after run(). Callbacks added before run() are merged into the controller when it is built. """ def stop(self) -> None: """Signal graceful shutdown after current episode.""" Properties @property def state(self) -> LoopState: """Current LoopState.""" @property def best_snapshot(self) -> Optional[PolicySnapshot]: """Best known PolicySnapshot.""" When the trial-search path runs, the best trial's weights are warm-started into the main agent via load_weights() before the full run begins, and all trial checkpoint directories are deleted afterward. Optimizer class Optimizer: """ Simplified entry point for training. Wraps RLOptimizer with sensible defaults. Parameters ---------- agent: A fully-constructed agent from make_agent() or built manually. env: A Gymnasium environment. Used for window_size estimation and as the training environment when n_envs=1. n_envs: Number of parallel environments. When >1, pass env as a callable (``lambda: gym.make("EnvName")``) or a list of callables. window_size: Number of steps per training window. When None, computed automatically from env and agent type. max_episodes: Stop after this many episodes. None means run indefinitely. callbacks: Additional LoopCallback instances to attach. rollback_on_degradation: Roll back to the best checkpoint when performance degrades. checkpoint_dir: Directory for saving policy snapshots. kwargs: Additional keyword arguments forwarded to RLOptimizer. """ def __init__( self, agent, env, n_envs: int = 1, window_size: Optional[int] = None, max_episodes: Optional[int] = None, callbacks: Optional[List] = None, rollback_on_degradation: bool = False, checkpoint_dir: str = "./tensor_optix_checkpoints", optimizer=None, loss="auto", batch_size: int = 64, shuffle: bool = True, **kwargs, ): ... def run(self): """Start training. Blocks until max_episodes or KeyboardInterrupt.""" Optimizer auto-detects ML mode : if agent is an nn.Module (and not a BaseAgent ) and env is a torch.utils.data.Dataset or DataLoader , it builds an MLAgent + DatasetPipeline instead of an RL pipeline. See ML mode . For the RL path, it: Infers the algorithm name from the agent's class name (for window-size lookup): "ppo" if "ppo" or "graph" is in the class name, "sac" , "td3" , "dqn" / "rainbow" , else falls back on agent.is_on_policy . Computes window_size via optimal_window_size(env, algorithm=alg_name) if not given explicitly. Builds BatchPipeline ( n_envs=1 ) or VectorBatchPipeline ( n_envs>1 ). Collects any agent._neuroevo_callbacks (set by make_agent(..., neuroevo=True) ) and adds them to callbacks . Builds an SPSAOptimizer from agent.default_param_bounds unless optimizer= is passed explicitly or the agent declares no bounds (in which case SPSA is left inactive, with a warning logged). Assembles and stores an RLOptimizer . opt.run() simply delegates to the wrapped RLOptimizer.run() . Trial-search budget When agent_factory + pipeline_factory + param_space are given, run() first runs a TrialOrchestrator search. Each trial trains for max(1, int(max_episodes * trial_steps_fraction)) windows (30 windows when max_episodes is None ). RLOptimizer converts that to environment steps using the pipeline's step hint ( steps_per_episode , i.e. window_size for BatchPipeline and window_size * n_envs for VectorBatchPipeline ) before handing it to the orchestrator, whose trial_steps argument is in environment steps. Console output verbose=True output and the trial-search progress lines are written with an encoding-safe printer: on a stream that cannot represent the box-drawing/arrow glyphs (Windows cp1252 console, redirected stdout) they degrade to ? instead of raising UnicodeEncodeError . Finished-episode accounting RLOptimizer(min_completed_episodes_before_dormant=10) is forwarded to LoopController (also accepted under optimizer: in YAML configs). Windows in which no episode finished are trained on but not evaluated, and the loop cannot plateau before the minimum number of episodes has finished - see LoopController . This is independent of min_episodes_before_dormant , which counts windows .

docs.text: class RLOptimizer: """ Main public API. This is what users import. Assembles all components and delegates to LoopController. Sensible defaults for everything - minimal required args: agent, pipeline. Minimal usage: optimizer = RLOptimizer(agent=my_tf_agent, pipeline=my_pipeline) optimizer.run() With automatic trial-level hyperparameter search (TrialOrchestrator): optimizer = RLOptimizer( agent_factory=lambda params: MyAgent(params), pipeline_factory=lambda: MyPipeline(), param_space={ "learning_rate": ("log_float", 1e-4, 3e-3), "clip_ratio": ("float", 0.1, 0.3), }, n_trials=20, trial_steps_fraction=0.15, # 15% of max_steps per trial ) optimizer.run() # trial search runs first, then full training with best params When param_space + agent_factory + pipeline_factory are provided: 1. TrialOrchestrator runs n_trials independent short runs to find best params 2. agent_factory(best_params) creates the agent for the full run 3. The main RLOptimizer loop runs with those params + SPSA online adaptation The agent and pipeline args become optional when factories are provided. """
docs.title: RLOptimizer

docs.text: def __init__( self, agent: Optional[BaseAgent] = None, pipeline: Optional[BasePipeline] = None, evaluator: Optional[BaseEvaluator] = None, optimizer: Optional[BaseOptimizer] = None, checkpoint_dir: str = "./tensor_optix_checkpoints", max_snapshots: int = 10, rollback_on_degradation: bool = False, improvement_margin: float = 0.0, max_episodes: Optional[int] = None, base_interval: int = 1, backoff_factor: float = 2.0, max_interval_episodes: int = 100, plateau_threshold: int = 5, dormant_threshold: int = 20, degradation_threshold: float = 0.95, min_degradation_drop: float = 1e-4, noise_k: float = 2.0, score_window: int = 20, trend_window: int = 8, min_episodes_before_dormant: int = 0, min_episodes_before_degradation: int = 5, callbacks: Optional[List[LoopCallback]] = None, val_pipeline: Optional[BasePipeline] = None, score_smoothing: int = 2, checkpoint_score_fn=None, verbose: bool = False, verbose_log_file: Optional[str] = None, # ── DiagnosticController ── diag_loss_spike_factor: float = 5.0, diag_entropy_floor: Optional[float] = 0.05, diag_target_kl: Optional[float] = 0.02, diag_epsilon_patience: int = 20, diag_epsilon_reset_value: float = 0.3, diag_epsilon_score_threshold: float = 20.0, diag_min_episodes: int = 5, min_consecutive_degradations: int = 3, convergence_patience: int = 5, cv_threshold: float = 0.05, gap_threshold: float = 0.20, target_score: Optional[float] = None, # ── Trial-level search (TrialOrchestrator) ── agent_factory: Optional[Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], BaseAgent]] = None, pipeline_factory: Optional[Callable[[], BasePipeline]] = None, param_space: Optional[Dict[str, tuple]] = None, n_trials: int = 20, trial_steps_fraction: float = 0.01, val_pipeline_factory: Optional[Callable[[], BasePipeline]] = None, trial_agent_factory: Optional[Callable[[Dict[str, Any]], BaseAgent]] = None, ) Either agent or agent_factory must be provided, and either pipeline or pipeline_factory . RLOptimizer builds, internally: a TFEvaluator (default, if none given), an SPSAOptimizer seeded from the agent's default_param_bounds / default_log_params (if no optimizer given, or if a given SPSAOptimizer has no bounds yet), a CheckpointRegistry , a BackoffScheduler , and a DiagnosticController - then wraps them all in a LoopController . Off-policy agents ( agent.is_on_policy == False ) get more patient defaults automatically: if dormant_threshold is left at its default 20 , it's lowered to 15 ; if min_episodes_before_dormant is left at 0 , it's raised to agent.default_min_episodes_before_dormant (default 100 ).

docs.text: def run(self) -> None: """ Start the autonomous loop. Blocks until stopped or max_episodes reached. If param_space + agent_factory + pipeline_factory were provided: 1. Runs TrialOrchestrator to find best hyperparameter configuration. 2. Calls agent_factory(best_params) and pipeline_factory() to build the agent and pipeline for the full training run. 3. Runs the main loop with those params + SPSA online adaptation. """ def add_callback(self, cb: LoopCallback) -> None: """ Register an additional callback. Safe to call before or after run(). Callbacks added before run() are merged into the controller when it is built. """ def stop(self) -> None: """Signal graceful shutdown after current episode."""

docs.text: class Optimizer: """ Simplified entry point for training. Wraps RLOptimizer with sensible defaults. Parameters ---------- agent: A fully-constructed agent from make_agent() or built manually. env: A Gymnasium environment. Used for window_size estimation and as the training environment when n_envs=1. n_envs: Number of parallel environments. When >1, pass env as a callable (``lambda: gym.make("EnvName")``) or a list of callables. window_size: Number of steps per training window. When None, computed automatically from env and agent type. max_episodes: Stop after this many episodes. None means run indefinitely. callbacks: Additional LoopCallback instances to attach. rollback_on_degradation: Roll back to the best checkpoint when performance degrades. checkpoint_dir: Directory for saving policy snapshots. kwargs: Additional keyword arguments forwarded to RLOptimizer. """ def __init__( self, agent, env, n_envs: int = 1, window_size: Optional[int] = None, max_episodes: Optional[int] = None, callbacks: Optional[List] = None, rollback_on_degradation: bool = False, checkpoint_dir: str = "./tensor_optix_checkpoints", optimizer=None, loss="auto", batch_size: int = 64, shuffle: bool = True, **kwargs, ): ... def run(self): """Start training. Blocks until max_episodes or KeyboardInterrupt.""" Optimizer auto-detects ML mode : if agent is an nn.Module (and not a BaseAgent ) and env is a torch.utils.data.Dataset or DataLoader , it builds an MLAgent + DatasetPipeline instead of an RL pipeline. See ML mode . For the RL path, it: Infers the algorithm name from the agent's class name (for window-size lookup): "ppo" if "ppo" or "graph" is in the class name, "sac" , "td3" , "dqn" / "rainbow" , else falls back on agent.is_on_policy . Computes window_size via optimal_window_size(env, algorithm=alg_name) if not given explicitly. Builds BatchPipeline ( n_envs=1 ) or VectorBatchPipeline ( n_envs>1 ). Collects any agent._neuroevo_callbacks (set by make_agent(..., neuroevo=True) ) and adds them to callbacks . Builds an SPSAOptimizer from agent.default_param_bounds unless optimizer= is passed explicitly or the agent declares no bounds (in which case SPSA is left inactive, with a warning logged). Assembles and stores an RLOptimizer . opt.run() simply delegates to the wrapped RLOptimizer.run() .
docs.title: Optimizer

docs.text: When agent_factory + pipeline_factory + param_space are given, run() first runs a TrialOrchestrator search. Each trial trains for max(1, int(max_episodes * trial_steps_fraction)) windows (30 windows when max_episodes is None ). RLOptimizer converts that to environment steps using the pipeline's step hint ( steps_per_episode , i.e. window_size for BatchPipeline and window_size * n_envs for VectorBatchPipeline ) before handing it to the orchestrator, whose trial_steps argument is in environment steps.
docs.title: Trial-search budget

docs.text: verbose=True output and the trial-search progress lines are written with an encoding-safe printer: on a stream that cannot represent the box-drawing/arrow glyphs (Windows cp1252 console, redirected stdout) they degrade to ? instead of raising UnicodeEncodeError .

docs.text: RLOptimizer(min_completed_episodes_before_dormant=10) is forwarded to LoopController (also accepted under optimizer: in YAML configs). Windows in which no episode finished are trained on but not evaluated, and the loop cannot plateau before the minimum number of episodes has finished - see LoopController . This is independent of min_episodes_before_dormant , which counts windows .

docs.text: tensor_optix.optimizers Five concrete BaseOptimizer implementations. All operate in normalized [0, 1] parameter space. SPSAOptimizer class SPSAOptimizer: """ SPSA (Simultaneous Perturbation Stochastic Approximation) optimizer. Reference: Spall, J.C. (1992). "Multivariate Stochastic Approximation Using a Simultaneous Perturbation Gradient Approximation." All N bounded params are updated in exactly 2 episodes regardless of N, compared to BackoffOptimizer's 2N episodes (round-robin). Algorithm (all operations in normalized [0,1] param space): Episode 1 - PLUS probe: Sample Δ ∈ {-1, +1}^N (Rademacher vector) Apply x⁺ = clip(x + c·Δ, 0, 1) where c = perturbation_scale Record f⁺ (score after episode) Episode 2 - MINUS probe: Apply x⁻ = clip(x - c·Δ, 0, 1) Record f⁻ (score after episode) COMMIT (after episode 2): ĝᵢ = (f⁺ - f⁻) / (2c·Δᵢ) for each param i x_new_i = clip(x_i + α·ĝᵢ, 0, 1) θ_new_i = denormalize(x_new_i, lo_i, hi_i) where c = perturbation_scale (default 0.05), α = learning_rate (default 0.1). The Rademacher distribution minimises the variance of the gradient estimator for a given c (Spall 1992, Theorem 1). is_probing returns True during the plus and minus probe episodes so LoopController suppresses degradation detection. """ Constructor accepts param_bounds: dict[str, (lo, hi)] and log_params: set[str] (params normalized in log space - use for learning rates and anything spanning orders of magnitude). On improvement, probes shrink (avoid disrupting active learning); on plateau, probes widen (explore more aggressively) and the cycle restarts. If on_plateau() interrupts a cycle mid-probe, the next cycle starts from the interrupted cycle's base point x , not from the probe point x ± c·Δ the agent happens to hold at that moment - an unevaluated probe is never silently adopted as the new baseline. MomentumOptimizer class MomentumOptimizer: """ Adam-momentum finite-difference optimizer for hyperparameters. Gradient estimation - finite difference (probe/commit cycle): δᵢ = probe_scale × |θᵢ| gᵢ = (score_probe − score_base) / δᵢ Adam update in normalized [0,1] parameter space: mᵢ ← β₁·mᵢ + (1−β₁)·gᵢ (momentum) vᵢ ← β₂·vᵢ + (1−β₂)·gᵢ² (RMSProp) m̂ᵢ = mᵢ / (1 − β₁ᵗ), v̂ᵢ = vᵢ / (1 − β₂ᵗ) (bias correction) xᵢ ← clip(xᵢ + α · m̂ᵢ/√(v̂ᵢ+ε), 0, 1) Why Adam over plain finite-difference (BackoffOptimizer): - Momentum smooths noisy stochastic gradient estimates across episodes - Adaptive rates give consistent-gradient params larger steps - Exponential decay tracks a non-stationary landscape - Bias correction gives unbiased estimates from episode 1 """ def __init__( self, param_bounds, alpha=0.05, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8, probe_scale=0.05, min_delta=1e-8, ): """ Args: alpha: Step size in normalized [0,1] space (0.05 = max 5% of range per update). beta1: Momentum decay (0.9 = gradient EMA carries 90% of previous estimate). beta2: RMSProp decay (0.999 = long variance history, stable adaptive rates). probe_scale: Finite-difference step δ = probe_scale × |θ|. min_delta: Absolute minimum δ (prevents divide-by-zero when θ≈0). """ BackoffOptimizer class BackoffOptimizer: """ Staggered two-phase finite difference optimizer. Each bounded param gets its own independent probe/commit cycle, cycled round-robin. With N bounded params, a full cycle takes 2N episodes (probe + commit per param). Phase 1 - PROBE: x + δ (x - δ when x is already at the upper bound), record base_score. Phase 2 - COMMIT: improvement = probe_score - base_score improvement > 0 → keep the probe value improvement < 0 → step the other way from x (reflected step, clipped to the bounds - so a failed downward probe at the upper bound returns to x) improvement ≈ 0 → restore the pre-probe value x On improvement: increase perturbation_scale. On plateau: increase further, reset cycle. """ All probing happens in normalized [0,1] space - without normalization, perturbation_scale * |θ| collapses to min_delta for small-magnitude params. PBTOptimizer class PBTOptimizer: """ Pseudo Population-Based Training for single-agent use. Maintains a history of (HyperparamSet, primary_score) pairs as a virtual population (FIFO, last history_size entries, default 50). Exploit condition: if current_score < percentile(history_scores, 20): best_params = params from top 20% of history (by score) new_params = perturb(best_params, scale=small) Explore condition: else: new_params = perturb(current_params, scale=medium) Perturbation - two modes per parameter: Linear (default): new_val = clip(θ + uniform(-δ, +δ), low, high), δ = scale*(high-low) Log-scale (for log_scale_params, e.g. learning_rate): new_val = clip(θ * exp(uniform(-δ_log, +δ_log)), low, high) δ_log = scale * log(high / low) Equal probability mass per decade - correct for params spanning orders of magnitude (Jaderberg et al. 2017, PBT). """ AdaptiveOptimizer class AdaptiveOptimizer: """ Meta-optimizer that routes between SPSA, Momentum, Backoff, and PBT based on two mathematically grounded signals. Signal 1 - Lag-1 autocorrelation (ρ): ρ = Pearson_Corr(scores[t-1], scores[t]) over the recent window. ρ > +autocorr_threshold → smooth landscape → Momentum ρ < -autocorr_threshold → oscillating → Backoff (sign-only) |ρ| ≤ threshold → i.i.d. → SPSA Signal 2 - Relative performance gap (Δ): Δ = (current_score − historical_best) / |historical_best| (always ≤ 0) Δ < -gap_threshold → bad region of hyperparameter space → PBT Routing priority (first match wins): 1. Δ < -gap_threshold → PBT (escape bad region first) 2. ρ > +autocorr_threshold → Momentum (amplify smooth trend) 3. ρ < -autocorr_threshold → Backoff (tame oscillation) 4. otherwise → SPSA (default, balanced) Hysteresis: the active optimizer is held for at least switch_patience consecutive evals before any switch - a single unlucky episode cannot cause a regime change. All four sub-optimizers receive on_improvement/on_plateau callbacks regardless of which is active, so their internal state stays warm - switching is seamless with no cold-start penalty. """ @property def active_optimizer(self) -> str: """Name of the currently active sub-optimizer.""" See Tune hyperparameters online for usage guidance and a routing-condition summary table.

docs.text: tensor_optix.orchestrator TrialOrchestrator - Optuna-based trial-level hyperparameter optimization. This is a separate layer *above* RLOptimizer. It is NOT an online optimizer. Online optimizers (SPSA, BackoffOptimizer) adapt hyperparams *within* a single training run, episode by episode. Trial-level optimization (this module) runs N independent training trials, each with a different hyperparameter configuration drawn from a principled surrogate model (TPE). After all trials, the best configuration is identified and optionally used for a final full-budget training run. When to use each: - Use TrialOrchestrator to find a good starting configuration before committing to a long training run. - Use RLOptimizer (with SPSA) for online adaptation during the actual run. - They compose naturally: run TrialOrchestrator first, then pass the best params to RLOptimizer for the final run. Algorithm - Optuna TPE (Tree-structured Parzen Estimator): TPE models p(x | good) and p(x | bad) as kernel density estimates over past trial results, selecting the next configuration by maximising the expected improvement ratio. Mathematically equivalent to Bayesian optimisation with a non-parametric surrogate, without the O(n³) cost of GP inference. Used by Stable-Baselines3, CleanRL, and RLlib for RL HPO. Pruner - MedianPruner: after a warmup phase, prunes any trial whose intermediate score falls below the median of all trials at the same step - successive halving without a fixed budget assumption. Requires: optuna (optional dependency). pip install optuna ParamSpace ParamSpace = Dict[str, Tuple] Spec Meaning ("float", lo, hi) uniform float in [lo, hi] ("log_float", lo, hi) log-uniform float (good for learning rate) ("int", lo, hi) uniform int in [lo, hi] ("log_int", lo, hi) log-uniform int ("categorical", v1, v2, ...) one of the listed values TrialOrchestrator class TrialOrchestrator: """ Optuna-based trial-level hyperparameter optimizer for RLOptimizer. Each trial is a fully independent RLOptimizer run with a different hyperparameter configuration. Optuna's TPE sampler uses results from completed trials to choose better configurations for subsequent ones. Parameters ---------- agent_factory : Callable[[dict], BaseAgent] Called once per trial with the sampled param dict. Must return a freshly initialised agent (no shared state between trials). pipeline_factory : Callable[[], BasePipeline] Called once per trial. Must return a fresh pipeline instance. param_space : dict Maps param names to sampling specs (see ParamSpace). n_trials : int Number of independent trials to run. trial_steps : int Step budget per trial. Common heuristic: 10–20% of final training budget. direction : str "maximize" (default) or "minimize" for the primary score. n_startup_trials : int Random trials before TPE's surrogate model kicks in. Default 10. pruner_warmup_steps : int MedianPruner ignores scores before this many episodes. Default 5. pruner_interval : int MedianPruner checks every this many episodes. Default 1. optuna_verbosity : int Optuna log level. Default optuna.logging.WARNING. rloptimizer_kwargs : dict Extra kwargs forwarded to RLOptimizer for every trial. Do NOT pass max_episodes here - use trial_steps instead. val_pipeline_factory : Callable[[], BasePipeline], optional If provided, called once per trial to create a validation pipeline. checkpoint_score_fn : Callable[[BaseAgent], float], optional Forwarded to each trial's RLOptimizer. study_name, storage : str, optional Optuna study persistence (e.g. storage="sqlite:///optuna.db"). Default: in-memory (no persistence). """ def run(self) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], float]: """ Run all trials and return (best_params, best_score). Each trial: TPE suggests a config → fresh agent/pipeline built via factories → RLOptimizer runs for at most trial_steps env steps → best smoothed score reported to Optuna → MedianPruner may stop the trial early if the score is poor. The best trial's weights are accessible via best_weights_path. """ @property def best_weights_path(self) -> Optional[str]: """ Path to the best trial's saved weights directory. The caller is responsible for cleaning up run_ckpt_dir once weights have been loaded. """ @property def run_ckpt_dir(self) -> Optional[str]: """Root directory holding all trial checkpoints from the last run().""" @property def study(self) -> "optuna.Study": """The underlying Optuna study. Inspect trial history, plot, etc.""" @property def best_params(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]: ... @property def best_score(self) -> Optional[float]: ... def trials_dataframe(self): """Return a pandas DataFrame of all trial results (requires pandas).""" _IntermediateReporter (internal LoopCallback ) bridges RLOptimizer 's on_episode_end into Optuna's intermediate reporting - when Optuna's pruner raises TrialPruned , it's translated into a stop() call on the trial's RLOptimizer . See Run trial-level search for usage, including composing with RLOptimizer 's agent_factory / pipeline_factory / param_space constructor path.

Common heuristic: 10–20% of final training budget. direction : str "maximize" (default) or "minimize" for the primary score. n_startup_trials : int Random trials before TPE's surrogate model kicks in. Default 10. pruner_warmup_steps : int MedianPruner ignores scores before this many episodes. Default 5. pruner_interval : int MedianPruner checks every this many episodes. Default 1. optuna_verbosity : int Optuna log level. Default optuna.logging.WARNING. rloptimizer_kwargs : dict Extra kwargs forwarded to RLOptimizer for every trial. Do NOT pass max_episodes here - use trial_steps instead. val_pipeline_factory : Callable[[], BasePipeline], optional If provided, called once per trial to create a validation pipeline. checkpoint_score_fn : Callable[[BaseAgent], float], optional Forwarded to each trial's RLOptimizer. study_name, storage : str, optional Optuna study persistence (e.g. storage="sqlite:///optuna.db"). Default: in-memory (no persistence). """ def run(self) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], float]: """ Run all trials and return (best_params, best_score). Each trial: TPE suggests a config → fresh agent/pipeline built via factories → RLOptimizer runs for at most trial_steps env steps → best smoothed score reported to Optuna → MedianPruner may stop the trial early if the score is poor. The best trial's weights are accessible via best_weights_path. """ @property def best_weights_path(self) -> Optional[str]: """ Path to the best trial's saved weights directory. The caller is responsible for cleaning up run_ckpt_dir once weights have been loaded. """ @property def run_ckpt_dir(self) -> Optional[str]: """Root directory holding all trial checkpoints from the last run().""" @property def study(self) -> "optuna.Study": """The underlying Optuna study. Inspect trial history, plot, etc.""" @property def best_params(self) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]: ... @property def best_score(self) -> Optional[float]: ... def trials_dataframe(self): """Return a pandas DataFrame of all trial results (requires pandas).""" _IntermediateReporter (internal LoopCallback ) bridges RLOptimizer 's on_episode_end into Optuna's intermediate reporting - when Optuna's pruner raises TrialPruned , it's translated into a stop() call on the trial's RLOptimizer .
